title.en: Volume 60: Book of Wu 15 - Biographies of He, Quan, Lü, Zhou, and Zhongli
title.raw: 卷六十 吳書十五 賀全呂周鍾離傳 Volume 60: Book of Wu 15 - Biographies of He, Quan, Lü, Zhou, and Zhongli

sentences.zh: 賀齊字公苗，會稽山陰人也。

translations.literal: He Qi, courtesy name Gongmiao, was a man of Shanyin in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: He Qi, styled Gongmiao, came from Shanyin in Kuaiji commandery.

sentences.zh: 〈《虞预晋书》曰：贺氏本姓庆氏。

translations.literal: ( The Jin shu of Yu Yu states: The He clan originally bore the surname Qing.
translations.idiomatic: ( Yu Yu's Jin shu notes that the He family was originally surnamed Qing.

sentences.zh: 齐伯父纯，儒学有重名，汉安帝时为侍中、江夏太守，去官，与江夏黄琼、

translations.literal: Qi's paternal uncle Chun had great fame in Confucian learning; under Han Emperor An he was palace attendant and administrator of Jiangxia; leaving office, with Huang Qiong of Jiangxia,
translations.idiomatic: His uncle He Chun was a renowned Confucian who under Emperor An of Han had served as palace attendant and prefect of Jiangxia; after leaving office he was associated with Huang Qiong of Jiangxia,

sentences.zh: （汉中）

translations.literal: ( Hanzhong )
translations.idiomatic: ( Hanzhong )

sentences.zh: 〔广汉〕杨厚俱公车徵。

translations.literal: [ Guanghan ] Yang Hou were alike summoned by imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: and Yang Hou of Guanghan—all were summoned to court by imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 避安帝父孝德皇

translations.literal: To avoid the taboo on the name of Emperor An's father, the Filial Virtue Emperor,
translations.idiomatic: To avoid the personal name of Emperor An's father, posthumously titled the Filial Virtue Emperor,

translations.literal: ( emperor )
translations.idiomatic: ( emperor )

sentences.zh: 讳，改为贺氏。

translations.literal: they changed the surname to He.
translations.idiomatic: the clan changed its surname to He.

sentences.zh: 齐父辅，永宁长。〉

translations.literal: Qi's father Fu was magistrate of Yongning. )
translations.idiomatic: He Qi's father, He Fu, had been magistrate of Yongning. )

sentences.zh: 少為郡吏，守剡長。

translations.literal: In youth he served as a commandery clerk and acting magistrate of Shan.
translations.idiomatic: While still young he became a commandery clerk and acting magistrate of Shan county.

sentences.zh: 縣吏斯從輕俠為奸，齊欲治之。

translations.literal: The county clerk Si Cong practiced knightly bravado and did evil; Qi wished to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: A county clerk named Si Cong swaggered like a knight-errant and broke the law; He Qi meant to bring him to justice.

sentences.zh: 主簿諫曰：“從，縣大族，山越所附，今日治之，明日寇至。

translations.literal: The chief clerk remonstrated: "Cong is a great clan of the county; the mountain Yue attach themselves to him—if you punish him today, raiders will come tomorrow."
translations.idiomatic: The chief clerk warned him: "The Si are a powerful county clan, and the hill Yue rally to them—move against Si Cong today and you may face a raid tomorrow."

sentences.zh: ”齊聞大怒，便立斬眾。

translations.literal: Qi heard this and was greatly angry; at once he executed Cong before the assembled crowd.
translations.idiomatic: He Qi flew into a rage and had Si Cong beheaded on the spot before the crowd.

sentences.zh: 從族黨遂相糾合，眾千餘人，舉兵攻縣。

translations.literal: Cong's lineage and partisans thereupon gathered in alliance, more than a thousand men, raised arms and attacked the county.
translations.idiomatic: Si Cong's kinsmen and followers then mustered over a thousand men, took up arms, and stormed the county seat.

sentences.zh: 齊率吏民，開城門突擊，大破之，威震山越。

translations.literal: Qi led clerks and common people, opened the city gate and struck in a sudden rush, greatly defeated them, and his awesomeness shook the mountain Yue.
translations.idiomatic: He Qi led clerks and townsfolk, threw open the gates, and sallied forth in a shock attack that routed them—his name struck fear into the hill Yue.

sentences.zh: 後太末、豐浦民反，轉守太末長，誅惡養善，期用盡平。

translations.literal: Later the people of Tai and Fengpu rebelled; he was transferred to defend as magistrate of Tai, executed the wicked and nurtured the good, and within the allotted term all was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: When Tai and Fengpu rose in revolt, he was transferred to Tai as magistrate; he executed ringleaders, protected the innocent, and within his term had the region quiet again.

sentences.zh: 建安元年，孫策臨郡，察齊孝廉。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jian'an, when Sun Ce came to the commandery, he nominated Qi as filially pious and incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: In 196, when Sun Ce inspected the commandery, he nominated He Qi as xiaolian—filially pious and incorrupt.

sentences.zh: 時王朗奔東冶，侯官長商升為朗起兵。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Lang had fled to Dongye; the magistrate of Houguan, Shang Sheng, raised troops for Lang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lang had fled to Dongye, and Shang Sheng, magistrate of Houguan, raised troops in his support.

sentences.zh: 策遣永寧長韓晏領南部都尉，將兵討升，以齊為永寧長。

translations.literal: Ce sent the magistrate of Yongning, Han Yan, to lead the southern commandant and attack Sheng with troops, appointing Qi as magistrate of Yongning.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce sent Han Yan of Yongning to lead the southern commandant's force against Shang Sheng and named He Qi magistrate of Yongning.

sentences.zh: 晏為升所敗，齊又代晏領都尉事。

translations.literal: Yan was defeated by Sheng; Qi again replaced Yan in charge of the commandant's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yan lost to Shang Sheng; He Qi then took his place in command of the southern commandant.

sentences.zh: 升畏齊威名，遣使乞盟。

translations.literal: Sheng feared Qi's reputation and sent a messenger begging alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Sheng, cowed by He Qi's reputation, sent envoys suing for peace.

sentences.zh: 齊因告喻，為陳禍福，升遂送上印綬，出捨求降。

translations.literal: Qi therefore issued a proclamation explaining the matter and setting forth fortune and disaster; Sheng thereupon handed over his seals and ribbons, came out of his stockade, and sought to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He Qi issued a clear proclamation on the stakes; Shang Sheng surrendered his seals, left his fort, and submitted.

sentences.zh: 賊帥張雅、詹強等不願升降，反共殺升，雅稱無上將軍，強稱會稽太守。

translations.literal: The bandit chiefs Zhang Ya, Zhan Qiang, and others were unwilling to follow Sheng in submission; together they killed Sheng; Ya declared himself General Without Superior, Qiang declared himself administrator of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Bandit chiefs Zhang Ya and Zhan Qiang refused to follow Shang Sheng and killed him; Zhang Ya styled himself supreme general and Zhan Qiang declared himself prefect of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 賊盛兵少，未足以討，齊住軍息兵。

translations.literal: The bandits were strong and the troops few, not enough to attack; Qi halted the army and rested the troops.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels outnumbered him, so He Qi held his troops in check rather than risk a premature attack.

sentences.zh: 雅與女婿何雄爭勢兩乖，齊令越人因事交構。

translations.literal: Ya and his daughter's husband He Xiong contended for power and fell out; Qi ordered Yue people to stir trouble between them by exploiting events.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ya and his son-in-law He Xiong quarreled over precedence; He Qi had local Yue people play on the rift and widen it.

sentences.zh: 遂至疑隙，阻兵相圖。

translations.literal: It went so far as mutual suspicion and rift, blocked arms and plotted against each other.
translations.idiomatic: Suspicion hardened until the two factions faced each other under arms.

sentences.zh: 齊乃進討，一戰大破雅，強黨震懼，率眾出降。

translations.literal: Qi then advanced to attack; in one battle he greatly defeated Ya; Qiang's party was shaken with fear and led the host out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He Qi then struck, shattered Zhang Ya in a single battle, and Zhan Qiang's followers, terrified, came out en masse to surrender.

sentences.zh: 侯官既平。

translations.literal: With Houguan pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Houguan was now secure.

sentences.zh: 而建安、漢興、南平復亂，齊進兵建安，立都尉府，是歲八年也。

translations.literal: Yet Jian'an, Hanxing, and Nanping rebelled again; Qi advanced troops to Jian'an, set up a commandant's headquarters—it was the eighth year.
translations.idiomatic: But Jian'an, Hanxing, and Nanping rose again; He Qi marched on Jian'an, set up a command post there—it was the eighth year of the Jian'an era (203).

sentences.zh: 郡發屬縣五千兵，各使本縣長將之，皆受齊節度。

translations.literal: The commandery dispatched five thousand troops from subordinate counties, each county's magistrate leading them, all receiving Qi's orders.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery drafted five thousand men from its counties, each led by its own magistrate, all under He Qi's command.

sentences.zh: 賊洪明、洪進、苑御、吳免、華當等五人，率各萬戶，連屯漢興，吳五六千戶別屯大潭。

translations.literal: The bandits Hong Ming, Hong Jin, Yuan Yu, Wu Mian, Hua Dang—five men—each led ten thousand households, encamped in succession at Hanxing; Wu with five or six thousand households separately encamped at Da Tan.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel leaders Hong Ming, Hong Jin, Yuan Yu, Wu Mian, and Hua Dang—five chiefs—each commanded some ten thousand households in linked camps at Hanxing, while Wu led five or six thousand households in a separate camp at Great Pool.

sentences.zh: 鄒臨六千戶別屯蓋竹，大潭同出餘汗。

translations.literal: Zou Lin's six thousand households separately encamped at Gaizhu; Da Tan and the others issued forth from Yuhan.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Lin's six thousand households held Gaizhu; the Great Pool contingent and the others debouched from Yukan.

sentences.zh: 〈音干。〉

translations.literal: ( The character is read gan. )
translations.idiomatic: ( The gloss marks the place name Yukan with kan read like the word gan, "stem." )

sentences.zh: 軍討漢興，經餘汗。

translations.literal: The army marched on Hanxing and passed through Yuhan.
translations.idiomatic: The expedition route to Hanxing ran through Yukan.

sentences.zh: 齊以為賊眾兵少，深入無繼，恐為所斷，令松陽長丁蕃留備余汗。

translations.literal: Qi judged that the bandits were many and his troops few, that a deep thrust without follow-up risked being cut off; he ordered the magistrate of Songyang, Ding Fan, to remain and guard Yuhan.
translations.idiomatic: He Qi saw that the enemy outnumbered him and that a deep penetration without reserves risked encirclement; he ordered Ding Fan, magistrate of Songyang, to hold Yukan as a rear guard.

sentences.zh: 蕃本與齊鄰城，恥見部伍，辭不肯留。

translations.literal: Fan had been a neighboring magistrate with Qi and was ashamed to be placed under his command; he declined and was unwilling to stay.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Fan had been a peer magistrate alongside He Qi and resented serving under him; he refused the assignment.

sentences.zh: 齊乃斬蕃，於是軍中震慄。

translations.literal: Qi then executed Fan, whereupon the army was stricken with dread.
translations.idiomatic: He Qi had Ding Fan executed for insubordination, and the whole army took warning.

sentences.zh: 無不用命。

translations.literal: None did not obey orders.
translations.idiomatic: From then on no one dared disobey.

sentences.zh: 遂分兵留備，進討明等，連大破之。

translations.literal: He then divided troops to leave a guard and advanced against Ming and the others, repeatedly defeating them in great battles.
translations.idiomatic: He left detachments on guard and pressed the attack on Hong Ming and his allies, crushing them in successive battles.

sentences.zh: 臨陳斬明，其免、當、進、御皆降。

translations.literal: In battle he beheaded Ming; Mian, Dang, Jin, and Yu all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Ming died in the fighting; Wu Mian, Hua Dang, Hong Jin, and Yuan Yu surrendered.

sentences.zh: 轉擊蓋竹，軍向大潭，三將又降。

translations.literal: He swung to attack Gaizhu, marched toward Da Tan; three generals again surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He turned on Gaizhu, then advanced on Great Pool, where three more rebel chiefs yielded.

sentences.zh: 凡討治斬首六千級，名帥盡擒。

translations.literal: In all the campaigns he took six thousand heads and captured every noted chief.
translations.idiomatic: The campaigns yielded six thousand heads and every major leader was taken alive.

sentences.zh: 復立縣邑，料出兵萬人，拜為平東校尉。

translations.literal: He restored counties and settlements, assessed ten thousand men for levy, and was appointed Colonel Who Pacifies the East.
translations.idiomatic: He restored local administration, enrolled ten thousand men for service, and was promoted to Colonel Who Pacifies the East.

sentences.zh: 十年，轉討上饒，分以為建平縣。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he turned to attack Shangrao and divided off territory to establish Jianping county.
translations.idiomatic: In 205 he campaigned against Shangrao and carved out territory for a new Jianping county.

sentences.zh: 十三年，遷威武中郎將，討丹陽黟、歙。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was promoted to General of Majestic Might in the Guards and campaigned against Yi and She in Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: In 208 he was raised to General of Majestic Might in the Guards and sent against the Yi and She districts of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 時武強、葉鄉、東陽、豐浦四鄉先降，齊表言以葉鄉為始新縣。

translations.literal: At that time the four townships Wuqiang, Ye, Dongyang, and Feng had surrendered first; Qi memorialized that Ye township be made Shixin county.
translations.idiomatic: The four townships of Wuqiang, Ye, Dongyang, and Feng had already submitted; He Qi memorialized to elevate Ye township as Shixin county.

sentences.zh: 而歙賊帥金奇萬戶屯安勒山，毛甘萬戶屯烏聊山，黟帥陳僕，祖山等二萬戶屯林歷山。

translations.literal: While the She bandit chief Jin Qi with ten thousand households encamped Mount Anle, Mao Gan with ten thousand encamped Mount Wuliao, and the Yi chiefs Chen Pu, Zu Shan, and others with twenty thousand encamped Mount Linli.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the She leader Jin Qi camped ten thousand households on Mount Anle, Mao Gan another ten thousand on Mount Wuliao, and the Yi leaders Chen Pu and Zu Shan some twenty thousand on Mount Linli.

sentences.zh: 林歷山四面壁立，高數十丈，逕路危狹，不容刀楯，賊臨高下石，不可得攻。

translations.literal: Mount Linli was precipitous on all sides like a wall, several tens of ren high, paths narrow and dangerous, not admitting shield or blade; the bandits rained stones from the height and could not be attacked.
translations.idiomatic: Mount Linli rose like a sheer wall scores of feet high, with trails too narrow for shield or sword; the defenders rolled down boulders and seemed untakable.

sentences.zh: 軍住經日，將吏患之。

translations.literal: The army halted for days; officers and clerks worried over it.
translations.idiomatic: The siege stalled for days while officers fretted.

sentences.zh: 齊身出周行，觀視形便，陰募輕捷士，為作鐵弋，密於隱險賊所不備處，以戈拓斬山為緣道，夜令潛上，乃多縣布以援下人，得上百數人，四面流布，俱鳴鼓角，齊勒兵待之。

translations.literal: Qi personally went round and surveyed the favorable ground; secretly recruited nimble men, had iron grapnels made for them, in a hidden steep place where the bandits were unprepared used the grapnels to cut into the mountain and make a path by ropes, at night sent them up stealthily, then hung many lengths of cloth to haul men up; when over a hundred had reached the top they spread out on every side, all striking drums and blowing horns; Qi held the troops ready below.
translations.idiomatic: He Qi reconnoitered in person, picked agile climbers, forged iron hooks, and in a steep spot the enemy had left unwatched had them hack footholds and mount by ropes at night; cloth lines hauled up more than a hundred men, who then fanned out along the crest beating drums and blaring horns while He Qi waited below with the main body.

sentences.zh: 賊夜聞鼓聲四合，謂大軍悉已得上，驚懼惑亂，不知所為，守路備險者，皆走還依眾。

translations.literal: The bandits at night hearing drums on all sides thought the great army had all gained the summit; panic-stricken and confused, they knew not what to do; those guarding the paths and steep places all ran back to join the main mass.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing drums from every direction in the dark, the defenders assumed the whole army had gained the heights; panic spread, and pickets on the trails abandoned their posts to crowd the summit.

sentences.zh: 大軍因是得上，大破僕等，其餘皆降，凡斬首七千。

translations.literal: The great army thereby got up, greatly defeated Pu and the rest; the remainder all surrendered—in all seven thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: The main force then stormed the heights, shattered Chen Pu's band, and accepted the surrender of the rest—seven thousand heads in all.

sentences.zh: 〈《抱朴子》曰：昔吴遣贺将军讨山贼，贼中有善禁者，每当交战，官军刀剑不得拔，弓弩射矢皆还自向，辄致不利。

translations.literal: ( Baopuzi states: Formerly Wu sent General He against the mountain bandits; among the bandits was one skilled in "forbidding" magic—whenever battle joined, government troops could not draw swords, crossbows shot arrows that turned back on themselves—repeated ill success.
translations.idiomatic: ( The Baopuzi tells how Wu once sent General He against mountain bandits who knew "binding" magic: in battle government blades would not leave their scabbards and crossbow bolts would wheel about and strike the shooters—so the army kept losing.

sentences.zh: 贺将军长情有思，乃曰：“吾闻金有刃者可禁，虫有毒者可禁，其无刃之物，无毒之虫，则不可禁。

translations.literal: General He was thoughtful and said: "I have heard metal with an edge can be forbidden and creatures with venom can be forbidden; things without edge and insects without venom cannot be forbidden."
translations.idiomatic: General He reflected and said, "I am told edged metal can be bound and venomous creatures can be bound—but not edgeless things or stingless vermin."

sentences.zh: 彼必是能禁吾兵者也，必不能禁无刃物矣。

translations.literal: That must be one who can forbid our weapons—he cannot forbid things without edges.
translations.idiomatic: "Their sorcery can stop our blades—it cannot stop a club without an edge."

sentences.zh: ”乃多作劲木白棓，选有力精卒五千人为先登，尽捉棓。

translations.literal: He therefore had many hardwood white clubs made and picked five thousand strong crack troops as van, all with clubs.
translations.idiomatic: He had thousands of heavy wooden clubs cut and picked five thousand stout shock troops, each man armed with a club alone.

sentences.zh: 彼山贼恃其有善禁者，了不严备。

translations.literal: The mountain bandits relied on having the "forbidder" and were quite unprepared.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits trusted their magician and kept slack guard.

sentences.zh: 於是官军以白棓击之，彼禁者果不复行，所击杀者万计。〉

translations.literal: Thereupon government troops struck them with white clubs; the forbiddal truly no longer worked—those killed numbered in the tens of thousands. )
translations.idiomatic: When government troops fell on them with the clubs, the spells failed and the dead were counted in the tens of thousands. )

sentences.zh: 齊復表分歙為新定；

translations.literal: Qi again memorialized to divide She and establish Xinding,
translations.idiomatic: He Qi memorialized again to split off from She the new counties of Xinding,

sentences.zh: 黎陽、休陽。

translations.literal: Liyang, and Xiuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liyang, and Xiuyang counties.

sentences.zh: 並黟、歙凡六縣。

translations.literal: Altogether six counties including Yi and She.
translations.idiomatic: That made six counties in all, together with Yi and She.

sentences.zh: 權遂割為新都郡，齊為太守，立府於始新，加偏將軍。

translations.literal: Quan thereupon carved out as Xindu commandery; Qi became grand administrator, established headquarters at Shixin, and was promoted deputy general.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan thereupon formed Xindu commandery, made He Qi its grand administrator with his seat at Shixin, and added him the title of deputy general.

sentences.zh: 十六年，吳郡餘杭民郎稚合宗起賊，復數千人，齊出討之。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, the commoner Lang Zhi of Yuhang in Wu commandery, assembling his lineage, raised bandits—again several thousand strong—and Qi went out to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: In 211 Lang Zhi of Yuhang in Wu commandery rallied his lineage in revolt—several thousand strong—and He Qi marched against him.

sentences.zh: 即復破稚，表言分餘杭為臨水縣。

translations.literal: At once he again defeated Zhi and memorialized to divide Yuhang as Linshui county.
translations.idiomatic: He quickly broke Lang Zhi and memorialized to carve Yuhang into a new Linshui county.

sentences.zh: 被命詣所在，及當還郡，權出祖道，作樂舞象。

translations.literal: He received orders to go to his post, and when he was to return to the commandery, Quan came out on the road of leave-taking, holding music and elephant dance.
translations.idiomatic: When orders sent him to his post and he was due to return to the commandery, Sun Quan saw him off with music and an elephant dance.

sentences.zh: 〈吴书曰：权谓齐曰：“今定天下，都中国，使殊俗贡珍，狡兽卒舞，非君谁与？

translations.literal: ( Wu shu states: Quan said to Qi, "When we pacify All Under Heaven and set the capital in the Central Plains, so that strange lands offer tribute and sly beasts caper in the dance—who if not you will share it?"
translations.idiomatic: ( The Wu shu records Sun Quan saying to He Qi, "When the realm is settled and the capital fixed in the Central Plain, when distant peoples bring tribute and strange beasts dance in the court—who will stand at my side if not you?"

sentences.zh: ”齐曰：“殿下以神武应期，廓开王业，臣幸遭际会，得驱驰风尘之下，佐助末行，效鹰犬之用，臣之原也。

translations.literal: Qi said, "Your Highness in divine martialness answers the times and opens wide the royal enterprise; your servant has been fortunate to meet this conjunction and to gallop in the dust below, aiding in the least capacity and serving like hawk and hound—that is my sincere wish.
translations.idiomatic: He Qi replied, "Your Highness answers the age in godlike martial prowess and widens the royal work; I have only been lucky to ride in your dust, doing the least tasks like hawk or hound—that is all I could wish."

sentences.zh: 若殊俗贡珍，狡兽率舞，宜在圣德，非臣所能。”〉

translations.literal: If strange lands present tribute and sly beasts lead the dance, that belongs to sagely virtue—it is not what your servant could achieve." )
translations.idiomatic: As for tribute from afar and beasts capering in the hall—that will be the work of sage virtue, not anything your servant could claim." )

sentences.zh: 賜齊軿車駿馬，罷坐住駕，使齊就車。

translations.literal: He bestowed on Qi a light carriage and fine horses, dismissed the seated equipage, and made Qi mount the carriage alone.
translations.idiomatic: He bestowed on He Qi a light carriage and fine horses, dismissed the usual riding equipage, and had him ride alone.

sentences.zh: 齊辭不敢，權使左右扶齊上車，令導吏卒兵騎，如在郡儀。

translations.literal: Qi declined and did not dare accept; Quan had attendants help Qi into the carriage and ordered escort clerks, soldiers, and riders to proceed as in the commandery ritual.
translations.idiomatic: He Qi demurred; Sun Quan had attendants lift him into the carriage and ordered escort, clerks, and cavalry to array themselves as for a grand administrator's progress.

sentences.zh: 權望之笑曰："人當努力，非積行累勤，此不可得。

translations.literal: Quan watched him with a smile and said: "A man must strive—without accumulated conduct and accumulated diligence, this cannot be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan watched him with a smile and called, "A man must strive—without long habit of duty and toil, such honor never comes."

sentences.zh: "去百餘步乃旋。

translations.literal: " He turned back only after a hundred-odd steps.
translations.idiomatic: " Only after another hundred paces did he turn back.

sentences.zh: 十八年，豫章東部民彭材、李玉、王海等起為賊亂，眾萬餘人。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, the commoners Peng Cai, Li Yu, and Wang Hai in the eastern part of Yuzhang rose and made bandit disorder—a host of more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In 213 Peng Cai, Li Yu, and Wang Hai raised a rebellion of over ten thousand men in eastern Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 齊討平之，誅其首惡，餘皆降服。

translations.literal: Qi attacked and pacified them, executed the leaders, and the rest all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He Qi crushed the rising, executed the ringleaders, and received the submission of the rest.

sentences.zh: 揀其精健為兵，次為縣戶。

translations.literal: He picked out the pick and stout for the army and the next grade as county households.
translations.idiomatic: The ablest he drafted into the army; the next grade he registered as county households.

sentences.zh: 遷奮武將軍。

translations.literal: He was promoted General Who Displays Martial Might.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General Who Displays Martial Might.

sentences.zh: 二十年，從權征合肥。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he followed Quan on campaign against Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: In 215 he accompanied Sun Quan on the Hefei campaign.

sentences.zh: 時城中出戰，徐盛被創失矛，齊引兵拒擊，得盛所失。

translations.literal: At that time those in the city came out to fight; Xu Sheng was wounded and lost his spear; Qi led troops to meet and strike them and recovered Sheng's lost weapon.
translations.idiomatic: When the garrison sallied out, Xu Sheng was wounded and dropped his spear; He Qi countercharged and recovered it.

sentences.zh: 〈江表传曰：权征合肥还，为张辽所掩袭於津北，几至危殆。

translations.literal: ( Jiangbiao zhuan states: When Quan returned from the campaign against Hefei, Zhang Liao ambushed him north of the ford and he nearly met with peril and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: ( The Jiangbiao zhuan relates that on the return from Hefei Zhang Liao ambushed Sun Quan north of the crossing and nearly destroyed him.

sentences.zh: 齐时率三千兵在津南迎权。

translations.literal: At that time Qi had three thousand troops south of the ford to welcome Quan.
translations.idiomatic: He Qi had three thousand men waiting south of the ford to cover Sun Quan's withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 权既入大船，会诸将饮宴，齐下席涕泣而言曰：“至尊人主，常当持重。

translations.literal: When Quan had boarded the great ship, he met the generals in a drinking feast; Qi left his mat, weeping, and spoke: "The August Ultimate, lord of men, should always keep gravity.
translations.idiomatic: After Sun Quan boarded the flagship he feasted his generals; He Qi left his place weeping and said, "The sovereign of men must always keep his dignity.

sentences.zh: 今日之事，几至祸败，群下震怖，若无天地，原以此为终身诫。

translations.literal: As for today's matter, it nearly came to ruin and defeat; those below were shaken with terror as if heaven and earth had ceased—I pray you take this as a lifelong warning.
translations.idiomatic: What happened today nearly ended in disaster; every man aboard was terrified as if heaven and earth had failed—I beg you to take this as a warning for the rest of your life.

sentences.zh: ”权自前收其泪曰：“大惭！

translations.literal: Quan himself came forward, wiped away his tears, and said: "Great shame!
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan stepped forward, wiped his tears, and said, "I am deeply ashamed!

sentences.zh: 谨以克心，非但书诸绅也。”〉

translations.literal: I shall engrave this on my heart—not merely write it on my sash." )
translations.idiomatic: I will fix this in my heart—not merely tie a knot on my sash." )

sentences.zh: 二十一年，鄱陽民尤突受曹公印綬，化民為賊，陵陽、始安、涇縣皆與突相應。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, the commoner You Tu of Poyang received seals and ribbons from Duke Cao and converted the people into bandits; Lingyang, Shi'an, and Jing counties all responded to Tu.
translations.idiomatic: In 216 You Tu of Poyang took seals from Cao Cao and stirred the people to revolt; Lingyang, Shi'an, and Jing all rose with him.

sentences.zh: 齊與陸遜討破突，斬首數千，餘黨震服，丹楊三縣皆降，料得精兵八千人。

translations.literal: Qi with Lu Xun attacked and defeated Tu, took several thousand heads; the remaining adherents submitted in fear; three counties of Danyang all surrendered; he assessed eight thousand picked troops.
translations.idiomatic: He Qi and Lu Xun broke You Tu, took several thousand heads, and overawed the rest; three Danyang counties submitted, yielding eight thousand picked troops for the rolls.

sentences.zh: 拜安東將軍，封山陰侯，出鎮江上，督扶州以上至皖。

translations.literal: He was appointed General Who Secures the East, enfeoffed as marquis of Shanyin, went out to garrison the river, and supervised from Fuzhou upstream to Wan.
translations.idiomatic: He was named General Who Secures the East, enfeoffed as marquis of Shanyin, and sent to hold the Yangzi line from Fuzhou upstream to Wan.

sentences.zh: 黃武初，魏使曹休來伐。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huangwu, Wei sent Cao Xiu to attack.
translations.idiomatic: When the Huangwu era opened, Wei dispatched Cao Xiu against Wu.

sentences.zh: 齊以道遠後至，因住新市為拒。

translations.literal: Qi because the road was long arrived late and therefore halted at Xinshi to offer resistance.
translations.idiomatic: He Qi arrived late on the long march and therefore took position at Xinshi to block the enemy.

sentences.zh: 會洞口諸軍遭風流溺，所亡中分，將士失色，賴齊未濟，偏軍獨全，諸將倚以為勢。

translations.literal: It happened that the various armies at Dongkou suffered wind and flowing water—half were drowned; officers and soldiers lost color; they relied on Qi not yet having crossed—the detached force alone was whole—and the generals leaned on it for positional strength.
translations.idiomatic: When wind and current wrecked half the fleet at Dongkou, morale collapsed; only He Qi's column, still uncrossed, remained intact, and the other generals drew strength from it.

sentences.zh: 齊性奢綺，尤好軍事，兵甲器械極為精好，所乘船雕刻丹鏤，青蓋絳襜，干櫓戈矛，葩爪文畫，弓弩矢箭，咸取上材，蒙衝鬥艦之屬，望之若山。

translations.literal: Qi by nature loved luxuriant finery and especially loved military affairs; arms and equipment were extremely fine; the vessels he rode were carved in cinnabar and chased in gold, with green canopy and crimson screens, shield-arms, halberds and spears, floral talon patterns, bows and crossbows—all chosen from the finest timber; assault ships and fighting craft of that sort looked from afar like mountains.
translations.idiomatic: He Qi loved splendor and took special pride in his gear: arms and armor of the finest work, ships lacquered red and gold with green canopies and crimson curtains, carved rails, painted spears, and bows of choice wood—his war junks loomed on the water like hills.

sentences.zh: 休等憚之，遂引軍還。

translations.literal: Xiu and the others feared them and thereupon led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Xiu and his commanders took fright and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 遷後將軍，假節領徐州牧。

translations.literal: He was promoted General of the Rear, given credentials of authority as acting governor of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to General of the Rear, given the imperial baton, and made acting governor of Xu province.

sentences.zh: 初，晉宗為戲口將，以眾叛如魏，還為蘄春太守，圖襲安樂，取其保質。

translations.literal: At first Jin Zong had been general at Xikou; with his host he rebelled and went over to Wei, afterwards became grand administrator of Qichun, plotting to raid Anle and seize the hostages held there.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Zong had commanded at Xikou, defected to Wei with his troops, become prefect of Qichun, and schemed to strike Anle and seize hostages.

sentences.zh: 權以為恥忿，因軍初罷，六月盛夏、出其不意，詔齊督麋芳、鮮于丹等襲蘄春，遂生虜宗。

translations.literal: Quan took it as shame and rage; while the army had just stood down, in the sixth month of midsummer, issuing from their expectationlessness, he ordered Qi to supervise Mi Fang, Xianyu Dan, and others in a raid on Qichun—thereupon they captured Zong alive.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan burned with shame; while the army was barely rested, in the sixth month of high summer he sprang a surprise order on He Qi to lead Mi Fang, Xianyu Dan, and others in a swoop on Qichun that took Jin Zong alive.

sentences.zh: 後四年卒，子達及弟景皆有令名，為佳將。

translations.literal: Four years later he died; his sons Da and younger brother Jing both had fair reputation and were excellent generals.
translations.idiomatic: He died four years later; his sons He Da and He Jing both won renown as fine commanders.

sentences.zh: 〈会稽典录曰：景为灭贼校尉，御众严而有恩，兵器精饰，为当时冠绝，早卒。

translations.literal: ( Kuaiji dianlu states: Jing was Colonel Who Exterminates Bandits, strict yet kind toward the host he commanded, his weapons were exquisitely fitted—foremost of the age—he died early.
translations.idiomatic: ( The Kuaiji dianlu says He Jing served as Colonel Who Exterminates Bandits, ran a stern but fair camp, and outfitted his men with the finest arms of the day; he died young.

sentences.zh: 达颇任气，多所犯迕，故虽有征战之劳，而爵位不至，然轻财贵义，胆烈过人。

translations.literal: Da was rather headstrong and often gave offense, so though he had merit of campaigning his noble rank never rose high; yet he despised wealth and prized righteousness, bolder than common men.
translations.idiomatic: He Da was headstrong and often gave offense, so despite battlefield merit he never rose high in rank; yet he scorned riches and prized honor, with a courage beyond the common run.

sentences.zh: 子质，位至虎牙将军。

translations.literal: His son Zhi rose to the post of Tigergap General.
translations.idiomatic: His son He Zhi reached the post of Tigergap General.

sentences.zh: 景子邵，别有传。〉

translations.literal: Jing's son Shao has a separate biography. )
translations.idiomatic: He Jing's son He Shao has his own biography elsewhere. )

sentences.zh: 全琮字子璜，吳郡錢唐人也。

translations.literal: Quan Zong, courtesy name Zihuang, was a man of Qiantang in Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Zong, styled Zihuang, came from Qiantang in Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 父柔，漢靈帝時舉孝廉。

translations.literal: His father Rou was nominated as filially pious and incorrupt in the time of Han Emperor Ling.
translations.idiomatic: His father Quan Rou earned a xiaolian nomination under Emperor Ling of Han.

sentences.zh: 補尚書郎右丞，董卓之亂，棄官歸。

translations.literal: He was supplemented as gentleman of the palace, right aide; at the turmoil of Dong Zhuo he cast aside office and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a gentleman of the palace and right aide; when Dong Zhuo threw the capital into chaos he resigned and went home.

sentences.zh: 州辟別駕從事，詔書就拜會稽東部都尉。

translations.literal: The province summoned him as recorder on the staff of the chief clerk; an edict appointed him on the spot eastern commandant of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: The province engaged him as chief clerk's recorder; an imperial edict then named him eastern commandant of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 孫策到吳，柔舉兵先附，策表柔為丹楊都尉。

translations.literal: When Sun Ce reached Wu, Rou first raised troops and attached himself; Ce memorialized that Rou be made commandant of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Ce entered Wu, Quan Rou was first to rally and submit; Sun Ce had him appointed commandant of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 孫權為車騎將軍，以柔為長史，徙桂陽太守。

translations.literal: When Sun Quan was General of Chariots and Cavalry, he made Rou chief clerk and transferred him to grand administrator of Guilin.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Quan held the rank of General of Chariots and Cavalry, he made Quan Rou his chief clerk, then moved him to prefect of Guilin.

sentences.zh: 柔嘗使琮齎米數千斛到吳，有所市易。

translations.literal: Rou once sent Zong carrying several thousand hu of grain to Wu for trade.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Rou once sent his son Quan Zong to Wu with several thousand hu of grain to sell.

sentences.zh: 琮至，皆散用，空船而還。

translations.literal: When Zong arrived, he distributed it all in use and returned with empty boats.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Zong gave the grain away and sailed home with empty holds.

sentences.zh: 柔大怒，琮頓首曰：“愚以所市非急，而士大夫方有倒縣之患，故便振贍，不及啟報。

translations.literal: Rou was greatly angry; Zong knocked his head and said: "In my folly I thought what was bought was not urgent, while gentlemen of the court were suffering the affliction of an inverted gallows—I therefore hastened relief and had no time to report beforehand."
translations.idiomatic: Quan Rou raged; Quan Zong kowtowed and explained that the grain was not needed at once while refugees were starving—he had fed them first and failed to ask permission.

sentences.zh: ”柔更以奇之。

translations.literal: " Rou came instead to think him remarkable.
translations.idiomatic: " Quan Rou came to admire him for it.

sentences.zh: 〈徐众评曰：礼，子事父无私财，又不敢私施，所以避尊上也。

translations.literal: ( Xu Zhong comments: By ritual a son serving a father has no private property, nor dare he make private gifts—thereby to avoid slighting the honored above.
translations.idiomatic: ( Xu Zhong observes that ritual forbids a son private wealth or largesse toward others—lest he slight his father's authority.

sentences.zh: 弃命专财而以邀名，未尽父子之礼。

translations.literal: To cast aside life for wealth and thereby seek name does not exhaust the rite of father and son.
translations.idiomatic: To spend a father's grain chasing reputation falls short of true filial duty.

sentences.zh: 臣松之以为子路问“闻斯行诸？

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi considers: when Zilu asked, "On hearing this, shall I act?"
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi recalls Zilu's question, "When I hear a command, should I carry it out at once?"

sentences.zh: ”子曰“有父兄在”。

translations.literal: The Master said, "There are father and elder brother to consult."
translations.idiomatic: The Master answered, "Father and elder brothers still live—consult them first."

sentences.zh: 琮辄散父财，诚非子道，然士类县命，忧在朝夕，权其轻重，以先人急，斯亦冯暖市义、汲黯振救之类，全谓邀名，或负其心。〉

translations.literal: Zong thereupon scattered his father's wealth—truly it was not the way of a son; yet when gentlemen hung their lives in peril and worry lay from dawn to dusk, weighing light and heavy to put others' urgency first belongs with Feng Xuan buying righteousness for his lord or Ji An opening granaries to save the people—to call it wholly seeking name perhaps wrongs his intent. )
translations.idiomatic: Quan Zong had indeed overstepped a son's role—yet when scholars faced mortal need, to weigh the crisis and feed them first belongs with Feng Xuan's "buying righteousness" or Ji An's emergency relief; to dismiss it as mere fame-seeking may misread his heart. )

sentences.zh: 是時中州士人避亂而南，依琮居者以百數，琮傾家給濟，與共有無，遂顯名遠近。

translations.literal: At that time gentlemen of the central plain fled turmoil southward; those who depended on Zong and dwelt with him numbered in the hundreds, and Zong exhausted his house to supply them, sharing existence and want with them—thereupon his name shone far and near.
translations.idiomatic: Central-plain refugees then flocked south by the hundreds; Quan Zong emptied his storehouses to feed them and shared whatever he had, and his name spread far and wide.

sentences.zh: 後權以為奮威校尉，授兵數千人，使討山越。

translations.literal: Later Quan made him Colonel Who Rouses Might, gave him several thousand troops, and sent him to campaign against the mountain Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan later named him Colonel Who Rouses Might, gave him a few thousand men, and sent him against the hill Yue.

sentences.zh: 因開募召，得精兵萬餘人，出屯牛渚，稍遷偏將軍。

translations.literal: He thereupon opened recruitment and summons, obtained more than ten thousand picked troops, went out and encamped at Niuzhu, and was gradually promoted deputy general.
translations.idiomatic: He opened recruiting, raised over ten thousand veterans, encamped at Niuzhu, and rose step by step to deputy general.

sentences.zh: 建安二十四年，劉備將關羽圍樊、襄陽，琮上疏陳羽可討之計，權時已與呂蒙陰議襲之，恐事洩，故寢琮表不答。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Jian'an, Liu Bei's general Guan Yu besieged Fan and Xiangyang; Zong submitted a memorial setting forth the plan by which Yu could be attacked; Quan at the time had already secretly plotted with Lü Meng to strike him and feared the affair would leak, therefore shelved Zong's memorial and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: In 219 Guan Yu besieged Fan and Xiangyang; Quan Zong memorialized on how to crush him. Sun Quan was already plotting with Lü Meng in secret and feared discovery, so he filed the memorial away without reply.

sentences.zh: 及禽羽，權置酒公安。

translations.literal: When Yu had been captured, Quan set a wine feast at Gong'an.
translations.idiomatic: After Guan Yu was taken, Sun Quan held a victory banquet at Gong'an.

sentences.zh: 顧謂琮曰：“君前陳此，孤雖不相答，今日之捷，抑亦君之功也。

translations.literal: He turned to Zong and said: "You earlier set forth this; though I did not answer, today's victory is also your merit."
translations.idiomatic: He turned to Quan Zong and said, "You urged this campaign though I gave no answer—today's triumph owes something to you."

sentences.zh: ”於是封陽華亭侯。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he enfeoffed him as village marquis of Yanghua.
translations.idiomatic: " He thereupon enfeoffed Quan Zong as village marquis of Yanghua.

sentences.zh: 黃武元年，魏以舟軍大出洞口，權使呂範督諸將拒之，軍營相望。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huangwu, Wei sent a great fleet out of Dongkou; Quan sent Lü Fan to supervise the various generals in resisting them; their camps faced one another across the water.
translations.idiomatic: In 222 Wei launched a major naval thrust at Dongkou; Sun Quan put Lü Fan in command of the defense, and the two fleets lay opposite each other.

sentences.zh: 敵數以輕船抄擊，琮常帶甲仗兵，伺候不休。

translations.literal: The enemy several times with light boats raided and struck; Zong constantly wore armor and carried arms, keeping watch without rest.
translations.idiomatic: Wei repeatedly sent light craft to raid; Quan Zong stayed armored and under arms, watching without pause.

sentences.zh: 頃之，敵數千人出江中，琮擊破之，梟其將軍尹盧。

translations.literal: Before long several thousand of the enemy came out into the middle of the river; Zong attacked and defeated them and took the head of their general Yin Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Soon thousands of Wei boats entered midstream; Quan Zong smashed them and beheaded their general Yin Lu.

sentences.zh: 遷琮綏南將軍，進封錢唐侯。

translations.literal: Zong was promoted General Who Pacifies the South and advanced in fief to marquis of Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to General Who Pacifies the South and promoted to marquis of Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 四年，假節領九江太守。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was given credentials of authority and concurrent office as grand administrator of Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Huangwu he received the baton and became concurrent prefect of Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 七年，權到皖，使琮與輔國將軍陸遜擊曹休，破之於石亭。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, when Quan reached Wan, he sent Zong with General Who Supports the State Lu Xun to strike Cao Xiu and defeated him at Shiting.
translations.idiomatic: In 228 Sun Quan advanced to Wan and sent Quan Zong with Lu Xun against Cao Xiu; they routed him at Shiting.

sentences.zh: 是時丹楊、吳、會山民復為寇賊，攻沒屬縣，權分三郡險地為東安郡，琮領太守。

translations.literal: At that time the mountain people of Danyang, Wu, and Kuaiji again became bandits and raiders, capturing subordinate counties; Quan divided the perilous ground of three commanderies to make Dong'an commandery, and Zong held the post of grand administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Hill folk of Danyang, Wu, and Kuaiji rose again, seizing county seats; Sun Quan carved out the rugged parts of three commanderies as Dong'an and named Quan Zong its prefect.

sentences.zh: 〈吴录曰：琮时治富春。〉

translations.literal: ( Wu lu states: At the time Zong administered from Fuchun. )
translations.idiomatic: ( The Wu lu notes that Quan Zong governed from Fuchun. )

sentences.zh: 至，明賞罰。

translations.literal: When he arrived, he made clear rewards and punishments.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he enforced rewards and penalties with clarity.

sentences.zh: 招誘降附，數年中，得萬餘人。

translations.literal: He summoned and enticed surrender and attachment; within several years he obtained more than ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: He offered terms to defectors and within a few years enrolled over ten thousand followers.

sentences.zh: 權召琮還牛渚，罷東安郡。

translations.literal: Quan recalled Zong to Niuzhu and abolished Dong'an commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan recalled Quan Zong to Niuzhu and dissolved Dong'an commandery.

sentences.zh: 〈江表传曰：琮还，经过钱唐，脩祭坟墓，麾幢节盖，曜於旧里，请会邑人平生知旧、宗族六亲，施散惠与，千有馀万，本土以为荣。〉

translations.literal: ( Jiangbiao zhuan states: When Zong returned, passing through Qiantang, he repaired sacrifice at tombs, banners, canopies, and insignia shone in his old village; he invited townsmen, old acquaintances, lineage kin, and six degrees of kin, distributing bounty of more than a thousand myriads—the native place took it as glory. )
translations.idiomatic: ( The Jiangbiao zhuan says that on his way back Quan Zong stopped at Qiantang, tended ancestral graves in full panoply of office, and feasted old friends and kin, scattering over ten million in gifts—the county counted it an honor. )

sentences.zh: 黃龍元年，遷衛將軍、左護軍、徐州牧，

translations.literal: In the first year of Huanglong he was promoted Guard General, left Protector of the Army, and governor of Xu province,
translations.idiomatic: In 229 he became Guard General, left Protector of the Army, and governor of Xu province,

sentences.zh: 〈吴书曰：初，琮为将甚勇决，当敌临难，奋不顾身。

translations.literal: ( Wu shu states: At first, when Zong was a general he was very bold and decisive, facing the foe in crisis and not sparing his person.
translations.idiomatic: ( The Wu shu says Quan Zong began as a fierce front-line fighter who threw himself into danger without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 及作督帅，养威持重，每御军，常任计策，不营小利。

translations.literal: When he became a supervising commander he cultivated awe and kept weight; whenever he commanded troops he always relied on stratagems and did not chase petty gain.
translations.idiomatic: As a high commander he grew deliberate, nursed his authority, and fought by calculation rather than chasing petty advantage.

sentences.zh: 江表传曰：权使子登出征，已出军，次于安乐，群臣莫敢谏。

translations.literal: Jiangbiao zhuan states: Quan sent his son Deng on campaign; the army had already marched and halted at Anle; among the ministers none dared remonstrate.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangbiao zhuan adds that when Sun Quan sent Crown Prince Deng on expedition the host had already reached Anle and no minister dared object.

sentences.zh: 琮密表曰：“古来太子未尝偏征也，故从曰抚军，守曰监国。

translations.literal: Zong secretly memorialized: "Never in antiquity has the heir apparent gone on a partial expedition; hence the follower is called 'who pacifies the army' and the guardian 'who oversees the state.'"
translations.idiomatic: Quan Zong secretly wrote, "No crown prince in history has campaigned alone—that is why aides are called pacifiers of the army and overseers of the state."

sentences.zh: 今太子东出，非古制也，臣窃忧疑。

translations.literal: " Now the heir apparent goes east—it is not the ancient system; your servant privately harbors worry and doubt."
translations.idiomatic: " To send the heir east breaks precedent; I cannot help but worry."

sentences.zh: ”权即从之，命登旋军，议者咸以为琮有大臣之节也。〉

translations.literal: " Quan at once followed it, ordered Deng to wheel the army about; discussants all thought Zong had the integrity of a great minister. )
translations.idiomatic: " Sun Quan accepted at once, recalled the heir's army, and observers praised Quan Zong's ministerly backbone. )

sentences.zh: 尚公主。

translations.literal: He married a princess.
translations.idiomatic: He married an imperial princess.

sentences.zh: 嘉禾二年，督步騎五萬征六安，六安民皆散走，諸將欲分兵捕之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiahe he supervised fifty thousand foot and horse on campaign against Lu'an; the people of Lu'an all scattered and fled; the generals wished to divide troops to capture them.
translations.idiomatic: In 233 he led fifty thousand horse and foot against Lu'an; the populace fled, and his generals wanted to scatter in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 琮曰：“夫乘危僥倖，舉不百全者，非國家大體也。

translations.literal: Zong said: "To ride peril for lucky chance, to act when not a hundred percent secure, is not the great body of the state."
translations.idiomatic: Quan Zong said, "Risking the army on a gamble when nothing is certain is not how a state should behave."

sentences.zh: 今分兵捕民，得失相半，豈可謂全哉?縱有所獲，猶不足以弱敵而副國望也。

translations.literal: " Now to divide troops to hunt the people—gain and loss would be half—how can that be called secure? Even if something were taken, it would still not be enough to weaken the enemy and answer the state's hopes."
translations.idiomatic: " Splitting up to round up civilians would yield mixed results at best—hardly a sure thing. Even captures would not weaken Wei enough to match what the court expects."

sentences.zh: 如或邂逅，虧損非小，與其獲罪，琮寧以身受之。

translations.literal: If by mischance we met reverse, the loss would not be small; rather than incur blame, Zong would rather receive it on his person.
translations.idiomatic: A reverse could cost dearly; rather than invite censure on you all, I will bear the blame myself.

sentences.zh: 不敢徼功以負國也。”

translations.literal: I dare not seek merit to the harm of the state.
translations.idiomatic: I will not chase glory at the state's expense.

sentences.zh: 赤烏九年，遷右大司馬、左軍師。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Chiwu he was promoted Right Grand Marshal and Left Army Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: In 246 he became Right Grand Marshal and Left Army Mentor.

sentences.zh: 為人恭順，善於承顏納規，言辭未嘗切迕。

translations.literal: In person he was deferential and compliant, skilled at reading expression and accepting regulation; his words never sharply contradicted.
translations.idiomatic: He was humble and tactful, quick to read Sun Quan's mood and take correction; his speech never cut across the sovereign.

sentences.zh: 初，權將圍珠崖及夷州，皆先問琮。

translations.literal: At first, when Quan was about to invest Zhuya and Yizhou, he always first asked Zong.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Quan first planned expeditions to Zhuya and Yizhou, he always consulted Quan Zong first.

sentences.zh: 琮曰：“以聖朝之威，何向而不克?然殊方異域，隔絕障海，水土氣毒，自古有之，兵入民出，必生疾病，轉相污染，往者懼不能反，所獲何可多致？

translations.literal: Zong said: "With the awe of the sage court, what direction would not be conquered? Yet strange regions beyond the barrier sea, cut off by waves, have poisonous miasma and water as from old—the army enters and the people come out, sickness must arise and spread from one to another; those who go fear they cannot return—what can be gained in quantity?
translations.idiomatic: Quan Zong answered, "Your majesty could conquer anywhere—yet those islands beyond the sea breed foul vapors as always; troops land, people scatter, plague follows, and past fleets seldom return. What profit repays the risk?

sentences.zh: 猥虧江岸之兵，以冀萬一之利，愚臣猶所不安。

translations.literal: To risk wasting the soldiers on the river shore in hope of a one-in-ten-thousand gain—your foolish servant still finds it unsettling.
translations.idiomatic: To bleed the Yangzi garrisons for a remote gamble unsettles even a dull minister like me.

sentences.zh: ”權不聽。

translations.literal: " Quan would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: " Sun Quan would not listen.

sentences.zh: 軍行經歲，士眾疾疫死者十有八九，權深悔之。

translations.literal: The army marched a full year; officers and men died of pestilence nine in ten; Quan deeply repented it.
translations.idiomatic: The expedition lasted a year; nine tenths of the men died of disease, and Sun Quan bitterly regretted it.

sentences.zh: 後言次及之，琮對曰："當是時，群臣有不諫者，臣以為不忠。"

translations.literal: Later when talk touched on it, Zong answered: "At that time, if among the ministers there were any who did not remonstrate, your servant would have held them disloyal."
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the topic arose, Quan Zong said flatly, "Any minister who had not remonstrated then I would have judged disloyal."

sentences.zh: 琮既親重，宗族子弟並蒙寵貴，賜累千金，然猶謙虛接士，貌無驕色。

translations.literal: Zong having become intimate and weighty, lineage and younger kin together received favor and nobility, gifts cumulatively worth a thousand in gold—yet still he met gentlemen with modesty and his bearing showed no arrogance.
translations.idiomatic: As favorite minister his whole clan rose in rank and fortune beyond measure, yet he remained courteous to scholars and never wore pride on his face.

sentences.zh: 十二年卒，子懌嗣。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he died; his son Yi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 249; his son Quan Yi inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 後襲業領兵，救諸葛誕於壽春，出城先降，魏以為平東將軍，封臨湘侯。

translations.literal: Later Yi inherited command of troops, went to rescue Zhuge Dan at Shoucun, left the city first to surrender; Wei made him General Who Pacifies the East and enfeoffed him marquis of Linxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Yi later commanded troops to relieve Zhuge Dan at Shoucun, was first out of the city to defect, and Wei named him General Who Pacifies the East, marquis of Linxiang.

sentences.zh: 懌兄子禕、儀、靜等亦降魏，皆歷郡守列侯。

translations.literal: The sons of Yi's elder brother—Wei, Yi, Jing, and others—also surrendered to Wei, all serving as prefects and village marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Nephews of Quan Yi (sons of his elder brother)—Quan Wei, Quan Yi, Quan Jing, and others—also went over to Wei and became prefects or village marquises.

sentences.zh: 〈吴书曰：琮长子绪，幼知名，奉朝请，出授兵，稍迁扬武将军、牛渚督。

translations.literal: ( Wu shu states: Zong's eldest son Xu was known from youth, attended court audience, went out and received troops, was gradually promoted General Who Displays Martial Might and supervisor at Niuzhu.
translations.idiomatic: ( The Wu shu records Quan Zong's eldest son Quan Xu as famous young, a court attendant who took command and rose to General Who Displays Martial Might and Niuzhu garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 孙亮即位，迁镇北将军。

translations.literal: When Sun Liang assumed the throne, he was promoted General Who Guards the North.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sun Liang he became General Who Guards the North.

sentences.zh: 东关之役，绪与丁奉建议引兵先出，以破魏军，封一子亭侯，年四十四卒。

translations.literal: In the Dongguan campaign Xu with Ding Feng proposed leading troops out first to break the Wei army; he enfeoffed one son village marquis; he died at age forty-four.
translations.idiomatic: At Dongguan he and Ding Feng urged a preemptive strike that broke the Wei force; one son was enfeoffed village marquis; he died at forty-four.

sentences.zh: 次子寄，坐阿党鲁王霸赐死。

translations.literal: The second son Ji, for currying favor with the Prince of Lu Ba, was ordered to die by bestowal.
translations.idiomatic: The second son, Quan Ji, died by imperial order for abetting Prince Sun Ba of Lu.

sentences.zh: 小子吴，孙权外孙，封都乡侯。〉

translations.literal: The youngest son Wu, Sun Quan's maternal grandson, was enfeoffed village marquis of the capital district. )
translations.idiomatic: The youngest, Quan Wu, Sun Quan's grandson by a daughter, was enfeoffed village marquis of the metropolitan district. )

sentences.zh: 呂岱字定公，廣陵海陵人也，為郡縣吏，避亂南渡。

translations.literal: Lü Dai, courtesy name Dinggong, was a man of Hailing in Guangling; he served as commandery and county clerk and crossed south to flee turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Dai, styled Dinggong, came from Hailing in Guangling; he had been a local clerk before fleeing south from the wars.

sentences.zh: 孫權統事，岱詣幕府，出守吳丞。

translations.literal: When Sun Quan took charge of affairs, Dai went to headquarters and went out as assistant magistrate of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Quan began to rule, Lü Dai presented himself at headquarters and became assistant magistrate of Wu.

sentences.zh: 權親斷諸縣倉庫及囚系，長丞皆見，岱處法應問，甚稱權意，召署錄事，出補余姚長，召募精健，得千餘人。

translations.literal: Quan personally judged the granaries and prisons of the counties; magistrates and assistants all appeared; Dai's handling of law matched questions and greatly pleased Quan's intent; he was summoned to serve as recording clerk, went out supplemented as magistrate of Yuyao, recruited the pick and stout and obtained more than a thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan personally inspected county granaries and jails; Lü Dai's legal rulings won praise, so he was made recording clerk, then magistrate of Yuyao, where he raised over a thousand picked troops.

sentences.zh: 會稽東冶五縣賊呂合、秦狼等為亂，權以岱為督軍校尉，與將軍蔣欽等將兵討之，遂擒合、狼，五縣平定，拜昭信中郎將。

translations.literal: The bandits Lü He and Qin Lang of the five counties of eastern Kuaiji Dongye made disorder; Quan made Dai colonel of the army and with General Jiang Qin and others led troops against them; thereupon they captured He and Lang, the five counties were pacified, and he was appointed Colonel of Manifest Trust in the Center.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü He and Qin Lang rebelled across five eastern Kuaiji counties, Sun Quan made Lü Dai an army colonel; with Jiang Qin he crushed the rising, took both chiefs, and promoted Lü Dai to Colonel of Manifest Trust in the Center.

sentences.zh: 〈吴书曰：建安十六年，岱督郎将尹异等，以兵二千人西诱汉中贼帅张鲁到汉兴寋城，鲁嫌疑断道，事计不立，权遂召岱还。〉

translations.literal: ( Wu shu states: In the sixteenth year of Jian'an, Dai supervised colonel Yin Yi and others with two thousand troops west to lure the Hanzhong bandit chief Zhang Lu to Hanxing garrison city; Lu suspected and cut the road—the plan could not be set up—Quan thereupon recalled Dai. )
translations.idiomatic: ( The Wu shu notes that in 211 Lü Dai led two thousand men west to lure Zhang Lu of Hanzhong to Hanxing; Zhang Lu grew suspicious and blocked the route, so the ruse failed and Sun Quan recalled him. )

sentences.zh: 建安二十年，督孫茂等十將從取長沙三郡。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Jian'an he supervised ten generals including Sun Mao in following the capture of the three Changsha commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: In 215 he directed ten generals under Sun Mao in the seizure of the three Changsha commanderies.

sentences.zh: 又安成、攸、永新、茶陵四縣吏共入陰山城，合眾拒岱，岱攻圍，即降，三郡克定。

translations.literal: Again the clerks of Ancheng, You, Yongxin, and Chaling jointly entered Yincheng mountain, combined hosts to resist Dai; Dai besieged them, they at once surrendered, and the three commanderies were taken and settled.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks of Ancheng, You, Yongxin, and Chaling holed up in Yincheng mountain; Lü Dai besieged them, they yielded at once, and the three commanderies were secured.

sentences.zh: 權留岱鎮長沙。

translations.literal: Quan left Dai to garrison Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan left Lü Dai to hold Changsha.

sentences.zh: 安成長吳碭及中郎將袁龍等首尾關羽，復為反亂。

translations.literal: The magistrate of Ancheng Wu Yang and Colonel of the Gentlemen of the Palace Yuan Long and others linked head and tail with Guan Yu and again made rebellious disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yang of Ancheng and Palace Gentleman Yuan Long coordinated with Guan Yu and rose again.

sentences.zh: 碭據攸縣，龍在醴陵。

translations.literal: Yang held You county; Long was at Liling.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yang held You county while Yuan Long was at Liling.

sentences.zh: 權遣橫江將軍魯肅攻攸，碭得突走。

translations.literal: Quan sent General Who Crosses the River Lu Su to attack You; Yang broke through and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan sent Lu Su against You; Wu Yang broke out and escaped.

sentences.zh: 岱攻醴陵，遂禽斬龍。

translations.literal: Dai attacked Liling and thereupon captured and beheaded Long.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Dai took Liling, captured Yuan Long, and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 遷廬陵太守。

translations.literal: He was promoted grand administrator of Luling.
translations.idiomatic: He was named prefect of Luling.

sentences.zh: 延康元年，代步騭為交州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yankang he replaced Bu Zhi as inspector of Jiao province.
translations.idiomatic: In 220 he succeeded Bu Zhi as inspector of Jiao province.

sentences.zh: 到州，高涼賊帥錢博乞降，岱因承製，以博為高涼西部都尉。

translations.literal: When he reached the province, the bandit chief Qian Bo of Gaoliang begged to surrender; Dai on inherited authority made Bo western commandant of Gaoliang.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival the Gaoliang chief Qian Bo offered submission; Lü Dai, acting under mandate, named him western commandant of Gaoliang.

sentences.zh: 又鬱林夷賊攻圍郡縣，岱討破之。

translations.literal: Again the Yi bandits of Yulin attacked and besieged commandery and county seats; Dai attacked and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Yilin Yi tribes then besieged county seats; Lü Dai defeated them.

sentences.zh: 是時桂陽、湞陽賊王金合眾於南海界上，首亂為害，權又詔岱討之，生縛金，傳送詣都，斬首獲生凡萬餘人。

translations.literal: At that time the bandit Wang Jin of Guilin and Zhenyang combined hosts on the border of Nanhai, first making trouble and harm; Quan again ordered Dai against him; he bound Jin alive, sent him in bonds to the capital, and in heads and captives altogether exceeded ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jin of Guilin and Zhenyang then rallied on the Nanhai frontier; Sun Quan again sent Lü Dai, who took Wang Jin alive to the capital with over ten thousand counted kills and captives.

sentences.zh: 遷安南將軍，假節，封都鄉侯。

translations.literal: He was promoted General Who Secures the South, given credentials of authority, and enfeoffed village marquis of the capital district.
translations.idiomatic: He became General Who Secures the South, received the baton, and was enfeoffed village marquis of the metropolitan district.

sentences.zh: 交阯太守士燮卒，權以燮子徽為安遠將軍，領九真太守，以校尉陳時代燮。

translations.literal: When the grand administrator of Jiaozhi Shi Xie died, Quan made Xie's son Hui General Who Pacifies the Distance, concurrent grand administrator of Jiuzhen, and Palace Gentleman Chen Shi to replace Xie.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Xie of Jiaozhi died, Sun Quan named his son Shi Hui General Who Pacifies the Distance and prefect of Jiuzhen, with Chen Shi to replace Shi Xie as prefect of Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 岱表分海南三郡為交州，以將軍戴良為刺史，海東四郡為廣州，岱自為刺史。

translations.literal: Dai memorialized to divide the three commanderies south of the sea as Jiao province with General Dai Liang as inspector, and the four commanderies east of the sea as Guang province with Dai himself as inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Dai memorialized to split the southern coast into Jiao province under Dai Liang and the eastern coast into Guang province under himself.

sentences.zh: 遣良與時南入，而徽不承命，舉兵戍海口以拒良等。

translations.literal: He sent Liang and Shi south to enter, but Hui would not accept the command, raised troops and garrisoned the river mouth to resist Liang and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Liang and Chen Shi marched south, but Shi Hui defied orders, mobilized, and blocked the estuary against them.

sentences.zh: 岱於是上疏請討徽罪，督兵三千人晨夜浮海。

translations.literal: Dai thereupon submitted a memorial asking leave to punish Hui's crime, supervised three thousand troops day and night by float on the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Dai then memorialized for punitive authority, took three thousand men, and crossed by sea day and night.

sentences.zh: 或謂岱曰："徽藉累世之恩，為一州所附，未易輕也。

translations.literal: Someone said to Dai: "Hui relies on favor accumulated through generations and is what one province cleaves to—not easy to treat lightly."
translations.idiomatic: Advisers warned him, "Shi Hui rests on generations of local power—the province cleaves to him; do not underestimate the fight."

sentences.zh: "岱曰："今徽雖懷逆計，未虞吾之卒至，若我潛軍輕舉，掩其無備，破之必也。

translations.literal: " Dai said: "Now Hui though harboring a rebellious plan has not reckoned with my sudden arrival; if I secretly march with a light stroke and catch him unprepared, defeat is certain.
translations.idiomatic: " Lü Dai replied, "He plots rebellion but does not expect a sudden strike; a swift secret landing will break him.

sentences.zh: 稽留不速，使得生心，嬰城固守，七郡百蠻，雲合響應，雖有智者，誰能圖之?"遂行，過合浦，與良俱進。

translations.literal: To delay and not be swift, letting him take heart, man the walls in firm defense, while the seven commanderies and hundred Man answer like clouds and echo like sound—even if there were a wise man, who could scheme it?" He thereupon went, passed Hepu, and advanced together with Liang.
translations.idiomatic: If we tarry and let him fortify while the seven commanderies rally, even a genius could not pry him loose." He sailed on, passed Hepu, and joined Dai Liang.

sentences.zh: 徽聞岱至，果大震怖，不知所出，即率兄弟六人肉袒迎岱。

translations.literal: When Hui heard Dai had arrived, he was indeed greatly shaken with terror, knew not what to do, and at once led six brothers in the flesh to welcome Dai.
translations.idiomatic: When word came that Lü Dai had landed, Shi Hui panicked, stripped to the waist, and led his six brothers out to surrender.

sentences.zh: 岱皆斬送其首，徽大將甘醴，桓治等率吏民攻岱，岱奮擊大破之，進封番禺侯。

translations.literal: Dai beheaded them all and sent their heads; Hui's great generals Gan Li and Huan Zhi led clerks and people in attacking Dai; Dai struck with vigor and greatly defeated them, and he was advanced in fief to marquis of Panyu.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Dai executed them all and sent the heads; Shi Hui's generals Gan Li and Huan Zhi then attacked him, but Lü Dai crushed them and was promoted to marquis of Panyu.

sentences.zh: 於是除廣州，復為交州如故。

translations.literal: Thereupon Guang province was abolished and Jiao province was as before.
translations.idiomatic: Guang province was then abolished and Jiao province restored as one.

sentences.zh: 岱既定交州，復進討九真，斬獲以萬數。

translations.literal: When Dai had settled Jiao province, he again advanced to campaign against Jiuzhen, beheading and capturing to the count of myriads.
translations.idiomatic: After pacifying Jiao he campaigned into Jiuzhen, taking tens of thousands of heads and prisoners.

sentences.zh: 又遣從事南宣國化，暨徼外扶南、林邑、堂明諸王，各遣使奉貢。

translations.literal: Again he sent staff south to proclaim the state's transformation; reaching beyond the frontier Funnan, Linxiang, and Tangming each sent envoys bearing tribute.
translations.idiomatic: He sent aides south to spread imperial virtue; beyond the border Funan, Linyi, and Tangming each sent tribute missions.

sentences.zh: 權嘉其功，進拜鎮南將軍。

translations.literal: Quan praised his merit and promoted him General Who Guards the South.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan commended the feat and promoted him to General Who Guards the South.

sentences.zh: 黃龍三年，以南土清定，召岱還屯長沙漚口。

translations.literal: In the third year of Huanglong, because the southern lands were quiet and settled, he summoned Dai back to garrison the Ou mouth of Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: In 231, with the south quiet, Sun Quan recalled Lü Dai to hold the Ou ford of Changsha.

sentences.zh: 〈王隐《交广记》曰：吴后复置广州，以南阳滕脩为刺史。

translations.literal: ( Wang Yin's Jiao Guang ji states: Wu later re-established Guang province with Teng Xiu of Nanyang as inspector.
translations.idiomatic: ( Wang Yin's Jiao Guang ji notes that Wu later restored Guang province under Inspector Teng Xiu of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 或语脩虾须长一丈，脩不信，其人后故至东海，取虾须长四丈四尺，封以示脩，脩乃服之。〉

translations.literal: Someone told Xiu that shrimp whiskers were a zhang long; Xiu did not believe it; that man later purposely went to the Eastern Sea, took a shrimp whisker four zhang four chi long, sealed it to show Xiu, and Xiu then believed. )
translations.idiomatic: Someone told Teng Xiu that shrimp antennae could grow ten feet; he scoffed until a man brought back a specimen over fourteen feet long in a sealed box—then he believed. )

sentences.zh: 會武陵蠻夷蠢動，岱與太常潘浚共討定之。

translations.literal: It happened that the Man and Yi of Wuling stirred in folly; Dai with Grand Master of Ceremonies Pan Jun together attacked and settled them.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuling tribes rose, Lü Dai and Pan Jun jointly suppressed them.

sentences.zh: 嘉禾三年，權令岱領潘璋士眾，屯陸口，後徙蒲圻。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiahe, Quan ordered Dai to lead Pan Zhang's soldiers, encamp at Lukou, afterward moved to Puqi.
translations.idiomatic: In 234 Sun Quan put Lü Dai in command of Pan Zhang's troops at Lukou, later shifted him to Puqi.

sentences.zh: 四年，廬陵賊李桓、路合、會稽東冶賊隨春、南海賊羅厲等一時並起。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, the bandits Li Huan of Luling and Lu He, the bandit Suichun of eastern Kuaiji Dongye, and the bandit Luo Li of Nanhai rose together at one time.
translations.idiomatic: In 235 rebels struck at once: Li Huan and Lu He in Luling, Suichun in eastern Dongye, and Luo Li in Nanhai.

sentences.zh: 權復詔岱督劉纂、唐咨等分部討擊，春即時首降，岱拜春偏將軍，使領其眾，遂為列將，桓、厲等皆見斬獲，傳首詣都。

translations.literal: Quan again ordered Dai to supervise Liu Zuan, Tang Zi, and others in dividing forces to strike and attack; Suichun at once was first to surrender; Dai appointed Suichun deputy general and had him command his host, whereupon he became a ranked general; Huan, Li, and others were all beheaded or captured and their heads sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan ordered Lü Dai with Liu Zuan and Tang Zi to divide forces. Suichun surrendered at once; Lü Dai made him a deputy general. Li Huan, Luo Li, and the rest were killed or captured, and their heads went to the capital.

sentences.zh: 權詔岱曰：“厲負險作亂，自致梟首；

translations.literal: Quan edicted to Dai: "Li relied on peril to make disorder and brought on his own decapitation;
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan wrote to Lü Dai, "Luo Li trusted defiles to rebel and lost his head for it;

sentences.zh: 桓兇狡反覆，已降復叛。

translations.literal: Huan was fierce and cunning, turning and turning again—having surrendered he rebelled anew.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huan was treacherous and twice turned coat after submitting.

sentences.zh: 前後討伐，歷年不禽，非君規略，誰能梟之？

translations.literal: Front and back in punitive expeditions, through years he was not captured—without your planning and strategy, who could have taken his head?
translations.idiomatic: Year after year you could not catch him—without your strategy, who could have beheaded him?

sentences.zh: 忠武之節，於是益者。

translations.literal: The integrity of loyal martialness is thereby made the more manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Your loyal courage shines all the brighter for it.

sentences.zh: 元惡既除，大小震懾，其餘細類，掃地族矣。

translations.literal: With the chief villain already removed, great and small are shaken with fear; the remaining petty sorts are swept away as if dust.
translations.idiomatic: The ringleaders are gone, the rest cowed; the small fry are swept away like dust.

sentences.zh: 自今巳去，國家永無南顧之虞，三郡晏然，無怵惕之驚。

translations.literal: From now on, the state will forever have no worry of looking south; the three commanderies are tranquil, without the alarm of fear and trembling.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth the south should give the court no further anxiety; three commanderies lie quiet, free of panic.

sentences.zh: 又得惡民以供賦役，重用歎息。

translations.literal: Again you have obtained wicked people to supply labor and tax service—We deeply sigh in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: You have also given us rebels to work the corvée and fields—We are deeply grateful.

sentences.zh: 賞不逾月，國之常典，制度所宜，君其裁之。”

translations.literal: Rewards not exceeding the month are the constant canon of the state; what institutions require, you shall weigh and decide.
translations.idiomatic: Prompt reward is the standing rule—decide the details of honors and pay as statute allows.

sentences.zh: 潘浚卒，岱代浚領荊州文書，與陸遜井在武昌，故督蒲圻。

translations.literal: When Pan Jun died, Dai replaced Jun in charge of Jing province paperwork, together with Lu Xun both at Wuchang, therefore supervising Puqi as before.
translations.idiomatic: After Pan Jun died, Lü Dai took his Jing province paperwork portfolio alongside Lu Xun at Wuchang and again oversaw Puqi.

sentences.zh: 頃之，廖式作亂。

translations.literal: Before long Liao Shi made disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Liao Shi rebelled.

sentences.zh: 攻圍城邑，零陵、蒼梧、鬱林諸郡騷擾，岱自表輒行，星夜兼路。

translations.literal: He attacked and besieged towns; Lingling, Cangwu, and Yulin commanderies were disturbed; Dai on his own authority memorialized that he would go at once, by starlight doubling the road.
translations.idiomatic: He besieged cities and threw Lingling, Cangwu, and Yulin into turmoil; Lü Dai asked leave to march at once, traveling night and day.

sentences.zh: 權遣使追拜岱交州牧，及遣諸將唐咨等駱驛相繼，攻討一年破之，斬式及遣諸所偽署臨賀太守費楊等，並其支黨，郡縣悉平，復還武昌。

translations.literal: Quan sent envoys to overtake and appoint Dai governor of Jiao province, and dispatched the generals Tang Zi and others in relays one after another; attacking and punishing for a year they broke them, beheaded Shi and the false-appointed grand administrator of Linhe Fei Yang whom he had set up and their partisans; commandery and county were all pacified, and he returned again to Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan caught up with orders naming Lü Dai governor of Jiao and sent Tang Zi and others in relays. A year of fighting broke the revolt: Liao Shi and Fei Yang, the puppet prefect of Linhe, were killed with their followers, order was restored, and Lü Dai returned to Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 時年已八十，然體素精勤，躬親王事。

translations.literal: At the time his years were already eighty, yet his person was by nature keen and diligent in attending to the king's business himself.
translations.idiomatic: He was eighty yet still ran day-to-day affairs with tireless care.

sentences.zh: 奮威將軍張承與岱書曰：

translations.literal: General Who Rouses Might Zhang Cheng wrote to Dai:
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cheng, General Who Rouses Might, wrote to Lü Dai:

sentences.zh: 昔旦奭翼同，《二南》作歌，今則足下與陸子也。

translations.literal: In olden days the Dan and Shi aided together, the Two Souths made song—today it is your foot and Master Lu.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shi once shared the Zhou ode of the Two Souths—you and Lu Xun stand in that same relation now.

sentences.zh: 忠勤相先，勞謙相讓，功以權成，化與道合，君子歎其德，小人悅其美。

translations.literal: Loyal diligence puts the other first, labor and modesty yield to each other; achievement is completed by weighing, transformation joins with the Way; gentlemen sigh at your virtue, petty men delight in your beauty.
translations.idiomatic: You vie in loyalty and modesty, balance power with Lu Xun, and join policy to the Way—gentlemen praise your virtue and commoners love your kindness.

sentences.zh: 加以文書鞅掌，賓客終日，罷不捨事，勞不言倦。

translations.literal: Add to that documents in constant handling, guests all the day, ceasing work without putting aside affairs, laboring without speaking of weariness.
translations.idiomatic: Add endless paperwork, guests from dawn to dusk, and you still never shirk a file or complain of fatigue.

sentences.zh: 又知上馬輒自超乘，不由跨躡，如此足下過廉頗也。

translations.literal: Again I know that when you mount a horse you always vault the mount yourself, not by way of stirrup—by this, my foot, you surpass Lian Po.
translations.idiomatic: They say you still vault into the saddle without stirrups—you put even Lian Po to shame.

sentences.zh: 何其事事決也。

translations.literal: How is it that in every affair you are so decisive?
translations.idiomatic: How can you be so decisive in everything you do?

sentences.zh: 《周易》有之，禮言恭，德言盛，足下何有盡此美耶！

translations.literal: The Zhou Changes has it: ritual speaks of reverence, virtue speaks of greatness—how can your foot have exhausted all this beauty!
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Changes pairs ritual with reverence and virtue with greatness—yet you seem to embody every excellence at once!

sentences.zh: 及陸遜卒，諸葛恪代遜，權乃分武昌為兩部，岱督右部，自武昌上至蒲圻。

translations.literal: When Lu Xun died, Zhuge Ke replaced Xun; Quan thereupon divided Wuchang into two parts; Dai supervised the right part, from Wuchang up to Puqi.
translations.idiomatic: After Lu Xun died, Zhuge Ke succeeded him; Sun Quan split Wuchang in two, putting Lü Dai in charge of the western sector from Wuchang up to Puqi.

sentences.zh: 遷上大將軍，拜子凱副軍校尉，監兵蒲圻，孫亮即位，拜大司馬。

translations.literal: He was promoted Grand Senior General, his son Kai was appointed deputy colonel of the army and supervised troops at Puqi; when Sun Liang assumed the throne, he was appointed Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Grand Senior General, son Lü Kai became deputy army colonel at Puqi, and under Sun Liang he was named Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 岱清身奉公，所在可述。

translations.literal: Dai kept his person pure in serving the public; wherever he went there was matter for narration.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Dai lived for the state; every post left a record worth telling.

sentences.zh: 初在交州，歷年不餉家，妻子饑乏。

translations.literal: At first in Jiao province, through years he did not send provisions home; wife and children hungered and lacked.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiao he sent no pay home for years; his wife and children went hungry.

sentences.zh: 權聞之歎息，以讓群臣曰：“呂岱出身萬里，為國勤事，家門內困，而孤不早知。

translations.literal: When Quan heard it he sighed and reproached the host of ministers, saying: "Lü Dai went out ten thousand li for the state's diligent service; inside the gates his household was in straits, yet I did not know it early.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan sighed and rebuked his ministers: "Lü Dai crossed ten thousand li in the state's service while his household starved, and I never knew."

sentences.zh: 股肱耳目，其責安在？

translations.literal: Thigh, arm, ear, and eye—where lies their responsibility?
translations.idiomatic: Where were you who are my eyes and ears?

sentences.zh: ”於是加賜錢米布絹，歲有常限。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he increased gifts of cash, grain, cloth, and silk, with a yearly fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: " He then granted Lü Dai a yearly stipend in coin, grain, cloth, and silk.

sentences.zh: 始，岱親近吳郡徐原，慷慨有才志，岱知其可成，賜巾□，與共言論，後遂薦拔，官至侍御史。

translations.literal: At first Dai drew near to Xu Yuan of Wu commandery, magnanimous and having talent and purpose; Dai knew he could be brought to completion, presented him headcloth and cap, discussed with him in speech, afterward thereupon recommended and raised him; his office reached palace attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Dai befriended Xu Yuan of Wu, a generous man of talent; he gave him cap and sash, talked policy with him, and recommended him until he reached palace censor.

sentences.zh: 原性忠壯，好直言，岱時有得失，原輒諫諍，又公論之，人或以告岱，岱歎曰："是我所以貴德淵者也。

translations.literal: Yuan by nature was loyal and stout, fond of straight speech; when Dai had gains and losses, Yuan always remonstrated and argued, again discussing it publicly; some told Dai; Dai sighed and said: "This is why I esteem Deyuan."
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yuan was blunt and loyal: whenever Lü Dai erred he remonstrated in public. When others tattled, Lü Dai said, "That is why I value Deyuan."

sentences.zh: "及原死，岱哭之甚哀。

translations.literal: " When Yuan died, Dai wept for him very mournfully.
translations.idiomatic: " When Xu Yuan died, Lü Dai mourned him bitterly.

sentences.zh: 曰：“德淵，呂岱之益友，今不幸，岱復於何聞過？

translations.literal: He said: "Deyuan was Lü Dai's beneficial friend; now that he is unfortunate, from whom shall Dai hear his faults?"
translations.idiomatic: He cried, "Deyuan was the friend who corrected my faults—now whom shall I hear them from?"

sentences.zh: ”談者美之。

translations.literal: " Discussants praised it.
translations.idiomatic: " Observers praised his integrity.

sentences.zh: 太平元年，年九十六卒，子凱嗣。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiping, at age ninety-six he died; his son Kai succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 256 at ninety-six; his son Lü Kai inherited his rank.

sentences.zh: 遣令殯以素棺，疏巾布□，葬送之制，務從儉約，凱皆奉行之。

translations.literal: He left instructions to be coffined in an unlacquered coffin, with plain headcloth and coarse cloth shroud; the regulations for burial and sending off were to follow utmost economy—Kai all carried them out.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered a plain coffin and simple grave clothes and asked for the cheapest funeral rites; Lü Kai obeyed every point.

sentences.zh: 周魴字子魚，吳郡陽羨人也。

translations.literal: Zhou Fang, courtesy name Ziyu, was a man of Yangxian in Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Fang, styled Ziyu, came from Yangxian in Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 少好學，舉孝廉，為寧國長，轉在懷安。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning, was nominated filially pious and incorrupt, was magistrate of Ningguo, transferred to be at Huai'an.
translations.idiomatic: He loved books from boyhood, earned a xiaolian nomination, served as magistrate of Ningguo, then moved to Huai'an.

sentences.zh: 錢唐大帥彭式等蟻聚為寇，以魴為錢唐侯相，旬月之間，斬式首及其支黨，遷丹楊西部都尉。

translations.literal: The great chief Peng Shi of Qiantang and others swarmed like ants to become bandits; Fang was made chancellor to the marquis of Qiantang; within a month or so he beheaded Shi's head and his partisans, and was promoted western commandant of Danyang.
