translations.idiomatic: When Peng Shi of Qiantang rallied bandits, Zhou Fang was named chancellor to the marquis of Qiantang; within a month he had Peng Shi's head and his gang, then rose to western commandant of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 黃武中。

translations.literal: In the Huangwu period.
translations.idiomatic: During the Huangwu era (222–229),

sentences.zh: 鄱陽大帥彭綺作亂，攻沒屬城，乃以魴為鄱陽太守，與胡綜戮力攻討，遂生禽綺，送詣武昌，加昭義校尉。

translations.literal: the great chief Peng Qi of Poyang made disorder, attacked and captured subordinate cities; Fang was therefore made grand administrator of Poyang; together with Hu Zong they joined strength in attack and punishment; thereupon they captured Qi alive and sent him to Wuchang; he was added Colonel of Manifest Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: the Poyang chief Peng Qi rebelled and seized towns. Zhou Fang became prefect of Poyang, joined Hu Zong in the campaign, took Peng Qi alive to Wuchang, and was given the title Colonel of Manifest Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 被命密求山中舊族名帥為北敵所聞知者，令譎挑魏大司馬揚州牧曹休。

translations.literal: He received orders secretly to seek among the mountain old clans and noted chiefs whom the northern foe had heard of, and order them to deceive and provoke Wei Grand Marshal and governor of Yang province Cao Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: He was secretly told to find mountain chiefs known to Wei who could bait Grand Marshal Cao Xiu of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 魴答，恐民帥小丑不足仗任，事或漏洩，不能致休，乞遣親人□箋七條以誘休。

translations.literal: Fang answered, fearing that minor people chiefs were not enough to rely on, the affair might leak and could not bring in Xiu; he begged to send a trusted kinsman with seven memorial strips to lure Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Fang replied that minor headmen might not be trusted and the plot could leak before Cao Xiu bit; he asked to send a kinsman with seven sealed letters to hook Cao Xiu.

sentences.zh: 其一曰："魴以千載饒幸，得備州民，遠隔江川，敬恪未顯，瞻望雲景，天實為之。

translations.literal: The first says: "Fang by a thousand years' lucky chance has been able to be a commoner of the province; far separated by rivers and streams, reverent respect has not yet been displayed; gazing at the cloud's aspect—Heaven has truly made it so.
translations.idiomatic: The first letter reads: "I am lucky enough to be a man of this commandery, yet the river keeps me from showing my respect; I can only look toward your clouds and trust Heaven's will.

sentences.zh: 精誠微薄，名位不昭，雖懷焦渴，曷緣見明?狐死首丘，人情戀本，而逼所制，奉覿禮違。

translations.literal: Sincerity is slight and thin, name and position are not clear; though I harbor burning thirst, by what thread can I be seen? The fox dies with its head toward its mound—human feeling clings to its root—yet I am pressed by what controls me, paying court and ritual are blocked.
translations.idiomatic: I am too obscure for you to notice my zeal; like the fox that dies facing its burrow, I long for home yet cannot cross to serve you.

sentences.zh: 每獨矯首西顧，未嘗不寤寐勞歎，展轉反側也。

translations.literal: Each time alone I crane my neck westward, never not waking and sleeping with laboring sighs, tossing and turning on my side.
translations.idiomatic: I crane my neck westward and sigh myself awake night after night.

sentences.zh: 今因隙穴之際，得陳宿昔之志，非神啟之，豈能致此!不勝翹企，萬里托命。

translations.literal: Now by the gap of a crack I obtain to set forth the ambition of long nights; if it were not the spirits opening the way, how could this be reached! I cannot overcome looking up in hope and entrusting my life ten thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Now a crack opens for me to voice an old dream—if not fate, what could bring it? I cast my life on you from a thousand leagues away.

sentences.zh: 謹遣親人董岑、邵南等托叛奉箋。

translations.literal: I respectfully send my kinsmen Dong Cen and Shao Nan, feigning rebellion to present the strips.
translations.idiomatic: I send my kinsmen Dong Cen and Shao Nan under cover of desertion to deliver this memorial.

sentences.zh: 時事變故，列於別紙，惟明公君侯垂日月之光，照遠民之趣，永令歸命者有所戴賴。"

translations.literal: The shifts of current affairs are set out on separate paper; only may the enlightened lord and marquis let fall the light of sun and moon, illumining the bent of a distant people, forever letting those who turn in their allegiance have something to lean on.
translations.idiomatic: The details are on a separate sheet; I beg your light to fall on a distant people so that we who would submit have something to lean on.

sentences.zh: 其二曰："魴遠在邊隅，江汜分絕；

translations.literal: The second says: "Fang is far at the border corner, the river marshes divide and cut off;
translations.idiomatic: The second says, "I am stranded beyond the river;

sentences.zh: 恩澤教化，未蒙撫及，而於山谷之間，遙陳所懷，懼以大義，未見信納。

translations.literal: favor's transforming instruction has not yet reached to comfort; yet in the midst of mountain valleys I set forth what I hold in my breast, fearing that on great principle I will not be believed and taken in.
translations.idiomatic: your grace has not yet reached me, yet I pour out my heart from the hills, fearing you will not believe me on mere principle.

sentences.zh: 夫物有感激，計因變生，古今同揆；

translations.literal: Things have feeling that stirs them; plans arise from change—ancient and modern share the measure;
translations.idiomatic: Feeling moves men and plans follow change—that has always been so;

sentences.zh: 魴仕東典郡，始願已獲，銘心立報，永矣無貳。

translations.literal: Fang served the east in administering a commandery; the first wish was already obtained; I engraved my heart to establish repayment—forever without a second.
translations.idiomatic: I have served Wu as prefect and won my first wish; I swore to repay you and will never waver.

sentences.zh: 豈圖頃者中被橫譴，禍在漏刻，危於投卵，進有離合去就之宜，退有誣罔枉死之咎，雖志行輕微，存沒一節，顧非其所，能不悵然!敢緣古人，因知所歸，拳拳輸情，陳露肝膈。

translations.literal: How did I reckon that lately I would meet with sudden blame, disaster in the space of a leak, danger like casting an egg—advancing there is the fitness of joining or leaving, retreating there is the fault of false accusation and wrongful death; though purpose and conduct are slight and mean, in preservation and destruction there is one principle—looking at it as not my place, how can I not be despondent! I dare follow the ancients in knowing where to return, with earnest heart laying bare liver and diaphragm.
translations.idiomatic: Then sudden blame struck—danger like an egg tossed on stone. To advance or flee, to live or die, I have but one resolve; I lay my heart bare as the ancients did in choosing a lord.

sentences.zh: 乞降春天之潤，哀拯其急，不復猜疑，絕其委命。

translations.literal: I beg the moistening spring of heaven, pityingly to save my extremity, no longer to harbor suspicion, to cut off my entrusting of life.
translations.idiomatic: I beg your spring rain of mercy to save me—do not doubt me, do not leave me to die untried.

sentences.zh: 事之宣洩。

translations.literal: If the affair should leak.
translations.idiomatic: If word leaks out,

sentences.zh: 受罪不測，一則傷慈損計，二則杜絕向化者心，惟明使君遠覽前世，矜而愍之，留神所質，速賜秘報。

translations.literal: Receiving punishment beyond measure—on the one hand it wounds compassion and harms planning, on the second it cuts off the hearts of those who would turn to transformation—only may the enlightened envoy lord look far at former ages, pity and commiserate, keep mind on what is pledged, and speedily grant a secret reply.
translations.idiomatic: punishment would wound kindness and choke future defectors. I beg you, wise envoy, read history, pity me, and answer in secret at once.

sentences.zh: 魴當候望舉動，俟須響應。"

translations.literal: Fang shall watch for movements and wait for the echoing response.
translations.idiomatic: I will watch for your move and answer it from within.

sentences.zh: 其三曰："魴所代故太守廣陵王靖，往者亦以郡民為變，以見譴責，靖勤自陳釋，而終不解，因立密計，欲北歸命，不幸事露，誅及嬰孩。

translations.literal: The third says: "The former grand administrator Wang Jing of Guangling whom Fang replaced—going back, he also because commandery people made change met with blame and reproach; Jing diligently explained himself yet in the end was not released; therefore he set up a secret plan wishing to return north in allegiance; unluckily the affair was exposed and execution reached even infants in arms.
translations.idiomatic: Third: my predecessor Wang Jing of Guangling was blamed when his people rioted; though he pleaded his case he was not cleared, plotted to defect north, was exposed, and even babes were killed.

sentences.zh: 魴既目見靖事，且觀東主一所非薄，□不復厚，雖或暫捨，終見翦除。

translations.literal: Fang has personally witnessed Jing's affair and moreover observes how the eastern lord in one place is thin and not again thick—though sometimes he temporarily sets aside, in the end he sees clipping and removal.
translations.idiomatic: I saw what happened to Wang Jing and I see how Sun Quan grows cold—he may spare you for a moment, but in the end he cuts you down.

sentences.zh: 今又令魴領郡者，是欲責後效，必殺魴之趣也。

translations.literal: Now again ordering Fang to lead the commandery is to desire to demand later effect—the bent of surely killing Fang.
translations.idiomatic: Now he makes me prefect again to test me—to kill me when I fail.

sentences.zh: 雖尚視息，憂惕焦灼，未知軀命，竟在何時。

translations.literal: Though still drawing breath, anxious fear scorches—unknown where body and life in the end rest in what time.
translations.idiomatic: I still breathe, but I burn with fear—I do not know how long I have to live.

sentences.zh: 人居世間，猶白駒過隙，而常抱危怖，其可言乎!惟當陳愚，重自披盡，懼以卑賤，未能採納。

translations.literal: Man dwells in the world like a white colt passing the crevice—yet constantly embracing peril and terror—how can it be spoken! Only ought I to set forth folly, again exhausting myself in disclosure, fearing that because of mean lowliness I cannot be taken in.
translations.idiomatic: Life is short as a white colt glimpsed through a crack, yet I live in terror. I lay out my folly though I may be too humble to be heard.

sentences.zh: 願明使君少垂詳察，忖度其言。

translations.literal: May the enlightened envoy lord slightly let fall detailed examination and weigh his words.
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to weigh my words with care.

sentences.zh: 今此郡民，雖外名降首，而故在山草，看伺空隙，欲復為亂。

translations.literal: Now the people of this commandery, though outwardly bearing the name of having surrendered heads, yet formerly are in mountain grass, watching for gaps and voids, wishing again to make disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The people here have bowed their heads but still lurk in the hills, watching for a chance to rise again.

sentences.zh: 為亂之日，魴命訖矣。

translations.literal: When the day of making disorder comes, Fang's fate is ended.
translations.idiomatic: When they rise again, I am a dead man.

sentences.zh: 東主頃者潛部分諸將，圖欲北進。

translations.literal: The eastern lord recently secretly divided and disposed the various generals, planning to wish to advance north.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern lord has lately been shifting generals northward in secret.

sentences.zh: 呂范、孫韶等入淮，全琮、朱桓趨合肥，諸葛瑾、步騭、朱然到襄陽。

translations.literal: Lü Fan and Sun Shao entered the Huai; Quan Zong and Zhu Huan hastened toward Hefei; Zhuge Jin, Bu Zhi, and Zhu Ran reached Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Fan and Sun Shao are on the Huai; Quan Zong and Zhu Huan press Hefei; Zhuge Jin, Bu Zhi, and Zhu Ran face Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 陸議、潘璋等討梅敷。

translations.literal: Lu Yi and Pan Zhang and others attacked Mei Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun (still named Lu Yi in court records) and Pan Zhang were dealing with Mei Fu.

sentences.zh: 東主中營自掩石陽，別遣從孫奐治安陸城，修立邸閣，輦貲運糧，以為軍儲，又命諸葛亮進指關西，江邊諸將無復在者，才留三千所兵守武昌耳。

translations.literal: The eastern lord's central camp itself screens Shiyang; separately he sent his cousin Sun Huan to secure Ancheng city, built lodges and treasuries, carted goods and transported grain to make military stores; again he ordered Zhuge Liang to advance pointing at west of the passes; the various generals along the river are none remaining—only about three thousand odd troops left guarding Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign masks Shiyang with his main body, sent Sun Huan to fortify Ancheng, built depots, moved grain for the army, and ordered Zhuge Liang westward; the river line is stripped—only three thousand men hold Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 若明使君以萬兵從皖南首江渚，魴便從此率厲吏民，以為內應。

translations.literal: If the enlightened envoy lord will take ten thousand troops from south of Wan to the head of the river isles, Fang will from this lead and rouse clerks and people to be inner responders.
translations.idiomatic: If you march ten thousand men from south of Wan to the river fords, I will stir the officials and people to rise within.

sentences.zh: 此方諸郡，前後舉事，垂成而敗者，由無外援使其然耳；

translations.literal: The various commanderies here, front and back in raising affairs, hung complete yet failed—because there was no outer aid to make it so;
translations.idiomatic: Past risings here failed for lack of outside help;

sentences.zh: 若北軍臨境，傳檄屬城，思詠之民，誰不企踵?願明使君上觀天時，下察人事，中參蓍龜，則足昭往言之不虛也。"

translations.literal: if the northern army presses the border and passes proclamations to subordinate cities, the people who think and chant—who will not stand on tiptoe? May the enlightened envoy lord above observe heaven's time, below examine human affairs, in the middle consult milfoil and tortoise—then it is enough to show that former words were not empty.
translations.idiomatic: if your host appears on the border and your proclamations reach the towns, every heart will lift. Read heaven, read men, read the oracles—you will see I do not lie.

sentences.zh: 其四曰："所遣董岑、邵南少長家門。

translations.literal: The fourth says: "The sent Dong Cen and Shao Nan, young and grown in the household gate.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth: "Dong Cen and Shao Nan were raised in my house.

sentences.zh: 親之信之，有如兒子。

translations.literal: Intimate with them and trusted them, as with sons.
translations.idiomatic: I love them like sons and trust them utterly.

sentences.zh: 是以特令□箋，托叛為辭，目語心計，不宣唇齒，骨肉至親，無有知者。

translations.literal: Therefore I especially ordered them to carry the strips, using rebellion as wording; eye language and heart calculation, not declared lip and teeth—even flesh and bone utmost kin have none who know.
translations.idiomatic: I gave them these letters under cover of defection; we need not speak aloud—even my kin know nothing.

sentences.zh: 又已敕之，到州當言往降，欲北叛來者得傳之也。

translations.literal: Again I have charged them that on reaching the province they shall say they go to surrender, wishing those who come north in rebellion to obtain transmission of it.
translations.idiomatic: I told them to claim they are defecting north so the story will spread.

sentences.zh: 魴建此計，任之於天，若其濟也，則有生全之福。

translations.literal: Fang established this plan, committing it to Heaven; if it succeeds, then there is the fortune of living preservation.
translations.idiomatic: I stake the plot on Heaven: success means life.

sentences.zh: 邂逅洩漏，則受夷滅之禍。

translations.literal: If by mischance it leaks, then one receives the calamity of extermination.
translations.idiomatic: A leak means extermination for us all.

sentences.zh: 常中夜仰天，告誓星辰。

translations.literal: Constantly at midnight I look up to Heaven, swearing oath to the stars and constellations.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight I swear to the stars.

sentences.zh: 精成之微，豈能上感，然事急孤窮，惟天是訴耳。

translations.literal: The subtlety of essence perfected—how can it move on high?—yet affairs are urgent and solitary and poor; only Heaven is the appeal.
translations.idiomatic: My prayer is too faint to move Heaven, yet in extremity I can only cry to the sky.

sentences.zh: 遣使之日，載生載死，形存氣亡，魄爽恍惚。

translations.literal: On the day of sending the messenger, bearing life bearing death, form exists and breath is gone, soul-spirit dazed and confused.
translations.idiomatic: The day the messengers left I was neither alive nor dead—body here, spirit adrift.

sentences.zh: 私恐使君未深保明，岑、南二人可留其一，以為後信。

translations.literal: Privately I fear the envoy lord has not deeply secured and made clear; of Cen and Nan two men one may be kept as later token of faith.
translations.idiomatic: If you still doubt me, keep one of the two messengers as hostage.

sentences.zh: 一□教還，教還故當言悔叛還首。

translations.literal: One messenger sent back, when instructed to return shall say he repents rebellion and returns head.
translations.idiomatic: Send one back with orders to pretend he repented and returned from defection.

sentences.zh: 東主有常科，悔叛還者，皆自原罪。

translations.literal: The eastern lord has a standing statute: those who repent rebellion and return are all themselves forgiven crime.
translations.idiomatic: Wu's law forgives any deserter who comes home—

sentences.zh: 如是彼此俱塞，永無端原。

translations.literal: like this each side is blocked and there is never an end or source.
translations.idiomatic: so both sides can keep the secret with no loose ends.

sentences.zh: 縣命西望，涕筆俱下。"

translations.literal: My fate looks west, tears and brush together descend.
translations.idiomatic: I look west and weep as I write.

sentences.zh: 其五曰："鄱陽之民，實多愚勁，帥之赴役。

translations.literal: The fifth says: "The people of Poyang are in truth many foolish and obstinate; leading them to go on corvée duty.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth: "The Poyang folk are stubborn; when you levy them,

sentences.zh: 未即應人，倡之為變，聞聲響抃。

translations.literal: they do not at once answer people's call; initiating them makes change; hearing sound they clap hands.
translations.idiomatic: they do not obey at once; stir them and they riot; they clap at rumor.

sentences.zh: 今雖降首，盤節未解，山棲草藏，亂心猶存。

translations.literal: Now though they have surrendered heads, tangled knots are not undone; they dwell in mountain and hide in grass; hearts of disorder still exist.
translations.idiomatic: Though they have yielded, the knot is not untied; they still hide in the hills with rebel hearts.

sentences.zh: 而今東主圖興大眾，舉國悉出。

translations.literal: Now again the eastern lord plans to raise a great host and the whole state marches out.
translations.idiomatic: Now the eastern lord means to empty the country for a great campaign.

sentences.zh: 江邊空曠，屯塢虛損，惟有諸刺奸耳。

translations.literal: The river bank is empty and vast; stockades and forts are hollow and diminished; only the various "pierce villain" agents remain.
translations.idiomatic: The river forts are hollow—only a few constables remain.

sentences.zh: 若因是際而騷動此民，一旦可得更會，然要恃外援，表裡機互，不爾以往，無所成也。

translations.literal: If by this opening you stir and move these people, in one morning you could again assemble them—yet it is essential to rely on outer aid, inner and outer working the machine in mutual fashion; not so, going as before, nothing is accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Strike now and you could rally them in a day—but you must coordinate from without; otherwise nothing comes of it.

sentences.zh: 今使君若從皖道進住江上，魴當從南對岸歷口為應。

translations.literal: Now if the envoy lord will advance by the Wan road and halt on the river, Fang shall from the south opposite bank at Likou be in response.
translations.idiomatic: If you march down from Wan and camp on the river, I will answer from Likou on the south bank.

sentences.zh: 若未徑到江岸，可住百里上。

translations.literal: If you do not go straight to the river bank, you may halt a hundred li above.
translations.idiomatic: If you cannot reach the bank, camp within a hundred li upstream.

sentences.zh: 令此間民知北軍在彼，即自善也。

translations.literal: Order the people here to know the northern army is there—that of itself is good.
translations.idiomatic: Let these people see your banners—that alone will steady them.

sentences.zh: 此間民非苦饑寒而甘兵寇，苦於征討，樂得北屬，但窮困舉事，不時見應，尋受其禍耳。

translations.literal: The people here are not suffering cold and hunger yet gladly taking up arms and raiding—they suffer from punitive expeditions and delight in belonging north; but poor and pressed in raising affairs, not timely seeing response, soon after receive its calamity.
translations.idiomatic: They do not love war for hunger's sake—they dread Wu's levies and would gladly serve the north if a northern host gave them hope.

sentences.zh: 如使石陽及青、徐諸軍首尾相銜，牽綴往兵，使不得速退者，則善之善也。

translations.literal: If you cause Shiyang and the armies of Qing and Xu to link head and tail, dragging and holding the troops gone south so they cannot speedily withdraw, then it is good in the good.
translations.idiomatic: If you can pin Shiyang and tie up Qing and Xu so Wu's northern army cannot pull back, that would be best of all.

sentences.zh: 魴生在江、淮，長於時事，見其便利，百舉百捷，時不再來，敢布腹心。"

translations.literal: Fang was born between the Yangzi and Huai, grew up knowing the affairs of the times, sees their convenience—a hundred tries, a hundred victories; the time does not come twice—I dare spread belly and heart.
translations.idiomatic: I was born between Yangzi and Huai; I know this ground—strike once, strike sure. The moment will not come twice; I lay my heart bare.

sentences.zh: 其六曰："東主致恨前者不拔石陽，今此後舉，大合新兵，並使潘浚發夷民，人數甚多，聞豫設科條，當以新羸兵置前，好兵在後，攻城之日。

translations.literal: The sixth says: "The eastern lord harbors hatred that formerly he did not take Shiyang; now this later undertaking greatly combines new troops and also orders Pan Jun to draft Yi people—the numbers are very many; hearing that beforehand he sets statutes and articles: he will place new weak troops in the van and good troops in the rear; on the day of attacking the city.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth: "Sun Quan still smarts over Shiyang; this new drive masses raw levies and drafts the Yi under Pan Jun. I hear he plans to put green troops in front and veterans behind when storming the walls.

sentences.zh: 雲欲以羸兵填塹，使即時破，雖未能然，是事大趣也。

translations.literal: He wishes to use weak troops to fill the ditches, making them at once broken through—even if it cannot be so, the affair has great tendency.
translations.idiomatic: He means to drive raw levies into your ditches to breach them at once; even if that fails, the thrust of the plan is clear.

sentences.zh: 私恐石陽城小，不能久留往兵，明使君速垂救濟，試宜疾密。

translations.literal: Privately I fear Shiyang city is small and cannot long detain the troops gone south; may the enlightened envoy lord speedily let fall rescue and relief—it is fitting to be swift and secret in trial.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyang is too small to hold your army long; you must rescue me quickly—and move with speed and secrecy.

sentences.zh: 王靖之變，其鑒不遠。

translations.literal: Wang Jing's change—its mirror is not far.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jing's fate is still a fresh lesson.

sentences.zh: 今魴歸命，非復在天，正在明使君耳。

translations.literal: Now Fang's turning in allegiance is no longer in Heaven—it rests squarely with the enlightened envoy lord.
translations.idiomatic: Whether I live or die now depends on you, not on fate.

sentences.zh: 若見救以往，則功可必成，如見救不時，則與靖等同禍。

translations.literal: If I see rescue by going forward, then merit can be surely completed; if I see rescue not timely, then I share calamity with Jing and the others.
translations.idiomatic: If you come in time we will succeed; if you delay, I share Wang Jing's end.

sentences.zh: 前彭綺時，聞旗麾在逢龍，此郡民大小歡喜，並思立效，若留一月日間，事當大成，恨去電速，東得增眾專力討綺，綺始敗耳。

translations.literal: Formerly at the time of Peng Qi, hearing that banners and standards were at Fenglong, the people of this commandery, great and small, rejoiced together and all thought to establish merit; if you had remained a month's space, the affair would have greatly succeeded—resentment that you went swift as lightning, the east was able to increase hosts and concentrate strength to punish Qi—only then did Qi begin to be defeated.
translations.idiomatic: When Peng Qi rebelled, your banners at Fenglong made every soul here rejoice; had you stayed one month the thing would have been won—but you withdrew like lightning, so Wu could mass troops and crush Peng Qi. Remember that.

sentences.zh: 願使君深察此言。"

translations.literal: May the envoy lord deeply examine this speech.
translations.idiomatic: Weigh these words carefully.

sentences.zh: 其七曰："今舉大事，自非爵號無以勸之，乞請將軍、侯印各五十紐，郎將印百紐，校尉、都尉印各二百紐，得以假授諸魁帥，獎厲其志，並乞請幢麾數十，以為表幟，使山兵吏民，目瞻見之，知去就之分己決，承引所救畫定。

translations.literal: The seventh says: "Now in raising a great affair, unless it be rank and title there is no means to encourage them; I beg fifty cords each of general and marquis seals, a hundred cords of colonel seals, two hundred cords each of commandant and commandant of the commandery seals, so as to be able to false-award the various chieftains and encourage their aims; and I beg several tens of banner and standard poles to serve as outward marks, so that mountain troops, clerks, and people seeing them with their eyes will know that the division of going and staying is already decided and the rescue you extend is drawn and fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh: "Great enterprises need titles to motivate men. Send fifty sets of general and marquis seals, a hundred colonel seals, two hundred each of commandant seals—so I can award them to hill chiefs—and send banners so everyone sees that sides are chosen and your rescue is sure.

sentences.zh: 又彼此降叛，日月有人，闊狹之間，輒得聞知。

translations.literal: Again each side in surrendering and rebelling has people daily and monthly; in the interval between wide and narrow I always obtain hearing and knowledge.
translations.idiomatic: Defections cross the line daily; I will hear every rumor in the gap between our armies.

sentences.zh: 今之大事，事宜神密，若省魴箋，乞加隱秘。

translations.literal: Now the great affair's circumstances ought to be spirit-like and secret; if you examine Fang's strips, I beg you add concealment and secrecy.
translations.idiomatic: Guard these letters as state secrets.

sentences.zh: 伏知智度有常，防慮必深，魴懷憂震灼，啟事蒸仍，乞未罪怪。"

translations.literal: I humbly know wisdom and measure have constancy, guard and consideration must be deep; Fang harbors worry scorched with anxiety, presenting affairs in steam again and again—I beg not yet to blame or marvel.
translations.idiomatic: I know you are wise and careful; forgive my repeated pleas and do not fault my anxiety.

sentences.zh: 魴因別為密表曰：

translations.literal: Fang therefore separately made a secret memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Fang also submitted a secret memorial to Sun Quan:

sentences.zh: 方北有逋寇，固阻河洛，久稽王誅，自擅朔土，臣曾不能吐奇舉善。

translations.literal: Fang north has the fugitive foe, firmly blocking the He and Luo, long delaying the king's punishment, arrogating himself to the northern soil—your servant has been unable to spit forth the strange and raise the good.
translations.idiomatic: North of us Cao Wei blocks the Central Plain and defies your punishment; I have done little to help.

sentences.zh: 上以光贊洪化，下以輸展萬一，憂心如搗，假寐忘寢。

translations.literal: Above to brighten and assist the vast transforming, below to extend in transport the one in ten thousand—worry is like pounding, false sleep forgets the couch.
translations.idiomatic: I would aid your great enterprise above and offer my mite below—my heart pounds and I cannot sleep.

sentences.zh: 聖朝天覆，含臣無效，猥發優命。

translations.literal: The sage court covers like heaven; containing your servant without effect, vulgarly issuing excellent command.
translations.idiomatic: Your court covers all like heaven; though I am unworthy you favored me with orders.

sentences.zh: 敕臣以前誘致賊休，恨不如計，令於郡界求山谷魁帥為北賊所聞知者。

translations.literal: Ordering your servant by the former to lure and bring in the bandit Xiu, hating that it did not match plan, now to seek within the commandery bounds mountain valley chieftains whom the northern bandits have heard and know.
translations.idiomatic: You first told me to lure Cao Xiu; that failed, so you ordered me to find hill chiefs known to Wei.

sentences.zh: 令與北通。

translations.literal: Order them to communicate north.
translations.idiomatic: You told me to link them to the north.

sentences.zh: 臣伏思惟，喜怖交集。

translations.literal: Your servant prostrate in thought—joy and terror cross together.
translations.idiomatic: I am torn between gratitude and fear.

sentences.zh: 竊恐此人不可卒得，假使得之，懼不可信，不如令臣譎休，於計為便。

translations.literal: Privately I fear this person cannot be got in haste; granting one could get him, I fear he cannot be trusted—it is not as good as ordering your servant to deceive Xiu—for planning it is convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Such men may not exist or may not be trusted; better let me deceive Cao Xiu myself.

sentences.zh: 此臣得以經年之冀願。

translations.literal: This is what your servant has been able to hope for through the years.
translations.idiomatic: That has been my wish for years.

sentences.zh: 逢值千載之一會，輒自督竭，竭盡頑蔽，撰立箋草以誑誘休者，如別紙。

translations.literal: Meeting the one meeting in a thousand years, I thereupon personally supervise exhaustion, exhausting stupid obscurity, composing and setting up strip drafts to deceive and lure Xiu—as on separate paper.
translations.idiomatic: This once-in-a-lifetime chance moves me to stake everything; I enclose the draft letters to bait Cao Xiu on another sheet.

sentences.zh: 臣知無古人單復之術，加卒奉大略，伀矇狼狽，懼以輕愚，忝負特施。

translations.literal: Your servant knows he has not the ancients' art of single and double; add to that suddenly receiving the great outline, muddled and embarrassed—I fear that in light foolishness I disgrace the special favor.
translations.idiomatic: I lack ancient strategists' subtlety; given your broad outline I stumble in the dark and fear my dull wits may shame your trust.

sentences.zh: 豫懷憂灼。

translations.literal: Beforehand I harbor worry scorched.
translations.idiomatic: I burn with anxiety beforehand.

sentences.zh: 臣聞唐堯先天而天弗違，博詢芻蕘，以成盛勳。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that Tang Yao was before Heaven yet Heaven did not oppose him; broadly inquiring of grass and firewood cutters, thereby to complete great merit.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Yao moved with heaven and still asked the humblest men—so great deeds are made.

sentences.zh: 朝廷神謨，欲必致休於步度之中，靈贊聖規，休必自送，使六軍囊括，虜無孑遺，威風電邁，天下幸甚。

translations.literal: The court's spirit-like plan desires surely to bring Xiu within the pace and measure; spirits assist the sage compass—Xiu will surely deliver himself, letting the six armies bag and capture, captives without a remnant, awesome wind and lightning in stride—under Heaven is greatly fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: Your divine plan will draw Cao Xiu into the trap; heaven will aid you—he will walk in and the six armies will bag him to the last man. The realm will rejoice.

sentences.zh: 謹拜表以聞，並呈箋草，懼於淺局，追用悚息。

translations.literal: I respectfully bow the memorial to inform, and together present strip drafts; fearing shallow scope, I pursue use with fearful panting.
translations.idiomatic: I submit this memorial with the enclosed drafts, trembling at my own shallow wit.

sentences.zh: 被報施行。

translations.literal: He received reply to put it into practice.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan approved the plan.

sentences.zh: 休果信魴，帥步騎十萬，輜重滿道，逕來入皖。

translations.literal: Xiu indeed trusted Fang, leading foot and horse one hundred thousand, baggage trains filling the road, going straight to enter Wan.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Xiu swallowed the bait, marched a hundred thousand horse and foot with baggage trains crowding the road, and drove straight into Wan.

sentences.zh: 魴亦合眾，隨陸遜橫截休，休幅裂瓦解，斬獲萬計。

translations.literal: Fang also combined hosts, following Lu Xun in crosswise cutting Xiu; Xiu split bolt and dissolved tile—beheaded and captured to the count of myriads.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Fang joined Lu Xun to cut him off; Cao Xiu's army shattered, with tens of thousands killed or taken.

sentences.zh: 魴初建密計時，頻有郎官奉詔詰問諸事，魴乃詣部郡門下，因下發謝，故休聞之，不復疑慮。

translations.literal: When Fang first set up the secret plan, frequently there were gentlemen of the palace bearing edicts interrogating on various matters; Fang thereupon went to the gate under the ministry command, thereupon let down hair in apology—therefore Xiu heard it and no longer doubted or worried.
translations.idiomatic: While the plot ripened, court envoys repeatedly questioned Zhou Fang; he went to the ministry gate and let his hair down in feigned disgrace—so Cao Xiu heard of his "fall" and doubted no more.

sentences.zh: 事捷軍旋，權大會諸將歡宴，酒酣。

translations.literal: When the affair succeeded and the army wheeled about, Quan greatly met the various generals in merry feast; wine was warm.
translations.idiomatic: After the victory Sun Quan feasted his generals deep into their cups.

sentences.zh: 謂魴曰：“君下發載義，成孤大事，君之功名，當書之竹帛。

translations.literal: He said to Fang: "You let down your hair bearing righteousness and completed my great affair; your merit and name ought to be written on bamboo and silk."
translations.idiomatic: He told Zhou Fang, "Your sham disgrace won me this victory—your name belongs on the bamboo slips."

sentences.zh: ”加裨將軍，賜爵關內侯。

translations.literal: " He added deputy general and bestowed the noble rank of marquis within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: " He made him deputy general and marquis within the passes.

sentences.zh: 〈徐众评曰：夫人臣立功效节，虽非一涂，然各有分也。

translations.literal: ( Xu Zhong comments: When a minister establishes merit and displays integrity, though it is not one path, yet each has its allotment.
translations.idiomatic: ( Xu Zhong remarks that ministers may serve in different ways, yet each role has its proper limit.

sentences.zh: 为将执桴鼓，则有必死之义，志守则有不假器之义，死必得所，义在不苟。

translations.literal: As general holding the drumstick and drum there is then the righteousness of certain death; as intent on defense there is then the righteousness of not borrowing tools; death must obtain its place—righteousness lies in not recklessness.
translations.idiomatic: A field general beats the drum and accepts death; a defender holds the wall without tricks; each death must be worthy.

sentences.zh: 鲂为郡守，职在治民，非君所命，自占诱敌，髡剔发肤，以徇功名，虽事济受爵，非君子所美。〉

translations.literal: Fang was grand administrator—his office lay in governing the people; without the lord's command he on his own accounted to lure the enemy, shaving and stripping hair and skin to pursue merit and name—though the affair succeeded and he received noble rank, it is not what gentlemen praise. )
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Fang was a prefect charged with civil rule, yet without orders he shaved his head to play traitor for glory—even though it worked, a gentleman does not call that beautiful. )

sentences.zh: 賊帥董嗣負阻劫鈔，豫章、臨川並受其害。

translations.literal: The bandit chief Dong Si relied on peril to rob and raid; Yuzhang and Linchuan together received his harm.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Dong Si held fastnesses and plundered Yuzhang and Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之案：孙亮太平二年始立临川郡，是时未有临川。〉

translations.literal: ( Your servant Songzhi considers: Sun Liang in the second year of Taiping first established Linchuan commandery—at this time there was not yet Linchuan. )
translations.idiomatic: ( Pei Songzhi notes that Linchuan commandery was not created until Sun Liang's Taiping 2—the text's Linchuan is an anachronism. )

sentences.zh: 吾粲、唐咨嘗以三千兵攻守，連月不能拔。

translations.literal: Wu Can and Tang Zi once with three thousand troops besieged him; connected months could not take him.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Can and Tang Zi besieged Dong Si with three thousand men for months without taking him.

sentences.zh: 魴表乞罷兵，得以便宜從事。

translations.literal: Fang memorialized begging to halt troops, obtaining to act as convenient from the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Fang asked leave to stop the siege and act on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 魴遣間諜，授以方策，誘狙殺嗣。

translations.literal: Fang sent spies, handing them stratagems, luring and ambushing to kill Si.
translations.idiomatic: He sent agents with a plan that lured Dong Si into an ambush and killed him.

sentences.zh: 嗣弟怖懼，詣武昌降於陸遜，乞出平地，自改為善，由是數郡無復憂惕。

translations.literal: Si's younger brother was frightened and fearful, went to Wuchang and surrendered to Lu Xun, begging to come out on flat ground and on his own reform to do good—thereby several commanderies had no more worry or fear.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Si's brother fled to Lu Xun at Wuchang, begged to settle on the plain and live honestly, and several commanderies were rid of fear.

sentences.zh: 魴在郡十三年卒，賞善罰惡。

translations.literal: Fang was in the commandery thirteen years, died, rewarding good and punishing evil.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Fang governed thirteen years until his death, always honoring the worthy and punishing the wicked.

sentences.zh: 威恩並行。

translations.literal: Awesome favor went side by side.
translations.idiomatic: Fear and kindness walked together in his rule.

sentences.zh: 子處，亦有文武材干，天紀中為東觀今、無難督。

translations.literal: His son Chu also had civil and martial talent and capacity; in the Tianji period he was director of the Eastern Pavilion and supervisor of the Garrison Without Difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhou Chu had both civil and martial gifts; under the Tianji era he became director of the Eastern Pavilion and colonel of the Garrison Without Difficulty.

sentences.zh: 〈《虞预晋书》曰：处入晋，为御史中丞，多所弹纠，不避强御。

translations.literal: ( Yu Yu's Jin shu states: When Chu entered Jin he became palace attendant censor, impeaching much and not avoiding the mighty.
translations.idiomatic: ( Yu Yu's Jin shu records that after entering Jin Zhou Chu became censor and struck at the powerful without flinching.

sentences.zh: 齐万年反，以处为建威将军，西征，众寡不敌，处临陈慷慨，奋不顾身，遂死於战场，追赠平西将军。

translations.literal: When Qi Wannian rebelled, they made Chu general Who Establishes Might for the western expedition; many could not match few; Chu facing battle was generous and moved, not sparing his person—thereupon he died on the battlefield; posthumously he was given General Who Pacifies the West.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi Wannian rose, Zhou Chu led the western campaign outnumbered; he fought boldly and died in the field, posthumously named General Who Pacifies the West.

sentences.zh: 处子飏、札，皆有才力，中兴之初，并见宠任。

translations.literal: Chu's sons Yang and Zha both had talent and force; at the beginning of the Restoration both saw favor and appointment.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Zhou Yang and Zhou Zha were able men favored at the start of the Eastern Jin restoration.

sentences.zh: 其诸子侄悉处列位，为扬土豪右，而札凶淫放恣，为百姓所苦。

translations.literal: His various sons and nephews were all at ranked posts, becoming leading magnates of Yang province, while Zha was fierce, lewd, and unrestrained, a suffering to the hundred surnames.
translations.idiomatic: His kin filled office and dominated Yangzhou while Zhou Zha ran wild and tormented the people.

sentences.zh: 泰宁中，王敦诛之，灭其族。〉

translations.literal: In the Taining period Wang Dun executed him and extinguished his clan. )
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun killed him in the Taining era and wiped out the clan. )

sentences.zh: 鍾離牧

translations.literal: Zhongli Mu
translations.idiomatic: Zhongli Mu

sentences.zh: 鍾離牧字子幹，會稽山陰人，漢魯相意七世孫也。

translations.literal: Zhongli Mu, courtesy name Zigan, was a man of Shanyin in Kuaiji, seventh-generation descendant of Han Lu minister of education Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongli Mu, styled Zigan, came from Shanyin in Kuaiji—the seventh generation from Zhongli Yi, minister of education to the Prince of Lu under Han.

sentences.zh: 〈会稽典录曰：牧父绪，楼船都尉，兄骃，上计吏，少与同郡谢赞、吴郡顾谭齐名。

translations.literal: ( Kuaiji dianlu states: Mu's father Xu was tower-ship commandant; elder brother Yin was clerk for presenting accounts—in youth with Xie Zan of the same commandery and Gu Tan of Wu commandery he shared one name.
translations.idiomatic: ( The Kuaiji dianlu says his father Zhongli Xu commanded tower ships; his brother Yin was an accounts clerk and in youth rivaled Xie Zan of Kuaiji and Gu Tan of Wu.

sentences.zh: 牧童龀时号为迟讷，骃常谓人曰：“牧必胜我，不可轻也。

translations.literal: In boyhood Mu was called slow and tongue-tied; Yin often told people: "Mu is sure to surpass me—do not treat him lightly."
translations.idiomatic: As a boy Mu seemed dull; his brother Yin warned others, "He will outshine me—do not underestimate him."

sentences.zh: ”时人皆以为不然。〉

translations.literal: " People of the time all thought it was not so. )
translations.idiomatic: " People did not believe him. )

sentences.zh: 少爰居永興，躬自墾田，種稻二十餘畝。

translations.literal: In youth he loved to dwell at Yongxing, personally opening fields and planting more than twenty mu of rice.
translations.idiomatic: He lived at Yongxing as a youth, clearing fields and planting over twenty mu of rice himself.

sentences.zh: 臨熟，縣民有識認之。

translations.literal: When it neared ripe, a county commoner recognized and claimed it.
translations.idiomatic: When the crop neared harvest a county man claimed the land was his.

sentences.zh: 牧曰：“本以田荒，故墾之耳。

translations.literal: Mu said: "Originally because the field was waste, therefore I opened it."
translations.idiomatic: Mu said, "I only farmed it because it lay waste."

sentences.zh: ”遂以稻與縣人。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he gave the rice to the county man.
translations.idiomatic: " He gave the whole crop to the man.

sentences.zh: 縣長聞之，召民繋獄，欲繩以法，牧為之請。

translations.literal: The county chief heard it, summoned the commoner and bound him in prison, wishing to rope him by law; Mu for his sake pleaded.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate jailed the claimant; Mu pleaded for him.

sentences.zh: 長曰：“君慕承宮，自行義事，

translations.literal: The chief said: "Sir, you admire Cheng Gong and on your own do deeds of righteousness,
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate said, "You imitate Cheng Gong's selfless ways,

sentences.zh: 〈《续汉书》曰：宫字少子，琅邪人，尝在蒙阴山中耕种禾黍，临熟，人就认之，宫便推与而去，由是发名，位至左中郎将、侍中。〉

translations.literal: ( Xu Han shu states: Gong, courtesy name Shaozi, was a man of Langya; he once planted millet in the mountains of Mengyin; when it neared ripe, people came and claimed it; Gong then pushed it to them and left; by this he rose to fame, reaching left gentleman of the palace and palace attendant. )
translations.idiomatic: ( The Continued Han shu tells of Cheng Gong of Langya, who gave away his mountain crop to a claimant and rose to high office. )

sentences.zh: 僕為民主，當以法率下，何得寢公憲而從君邪？

translations.literal: I am master for the people—ought to lead those below by law; how can I sleep on public statute and follow you?
translations.idiomatic: yet I must govern by law—how can I ignore the code for your sake?

sentences.zh: ”牧曰：“此是郡界，緣君意顧，故來蹔住。

translations.literal: " Mu said: "This is within the commandery bounds; because of the lord's kind regard I therefore came to dwell temporarily.
translations.idiomatic: " Mu replied, "This is your commandery; I only stayed here by your kindness.

sentences.zh: 今以少稻而殺此民，何心復留？

translations.literal: " Now for a little rice to kill this people—what heart would again remain?"
translations.idiomatic: " Would you execute a man over a little grain while I still wished to stay?"

sentences.zh: ”遂出裝，還山陰，長自往止之，為釋繋民。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he packed baggage and returned to Shanyin; the chief himself went to stop him, and for him released the bound commoner.
translations.idiomatic: " He packed to leave for Shanyin; the magistrate ran after him, freed the prisoner, and kept Mu.

sentences.zh: 民慚懼，率妻子舂所取稻得六十斛米，送還牧，牧閉門不受。

translations.literal: The commoner ashamed and afraid, led wife and children in pounding the taken rice and obtained sixty hu of polished rice, sent it back to Mu; Mu closed the gate and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed, the man and his family milled sixty hu of rice as repayment; Mu shut his gate and refused it.

sentences.zh: 民輸置道旁，莫有取者。

translations.literal: The common people transported and set it by the road side; none took it.
translations.idiomatic: They left the rice by the road; no one touched it.

sentences.zh: 牧由此發名。

translations.literal: Mu by this issued forth in name.
translations.idiomatic: From that his reputation spread.

sentences.zh: 〈徐众评曰：牧蹈长者之规。

translations.literal: ( Xu Zhong comments: Mu trod the gauge of the elder.
translations.idiomatic: ( Xu Zhong says Mu followed the elder's standard.

sentences.zh: 问者曰：“如牧所行，犯而不校，又从而救之，直而不有，又还而不受，可不谓之仁让乎哉？

translations.literal: The questioner said: "Such as Mu's conduct—offended yet not reckoning, again thereupon saving him, straight yet not possessing, again returning yet not accepting—can it not be called benevolent yielding?"
translations.idiomatic: A questioner asked, "Is that not perfect benevolence and yielding?"

sentences.zh: ”答曰：“异乎吾所闻。

translations.literal: " The answer said: "Different from what I have heard.
translations.idiomatic: " The answer was, "That is not what I call benevolence.

sentences.zh: 原宪之问於孔子曰：‘克伐怨欲不行焉，可以为仁乎？

translations.literal: Yuan Xian asked Confucius: "If conquering, boasting, resentment, and desire do not arise in him—can he be called benevolent?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xian asked whether a man who never boasts or nurses grudges is humane.

sentences.zh: ’孔子曰：‘可以为难矣，仁则吾不知也。

translations.literal: Confucius said: "That can be called difficult; as for benevolence, I do not know."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said that is hard; as for full humanity, he could not say.

sentences.zh: ’‘恶不仁者，其为仁矣。

translations.literal: " "To hate the not benevolent—that is benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: " To hate the inhumane is itself humanity."

sentences.zh: ’今小民不展四体，而认人之稻，不仁甚矣，而牧推而与之，又救其罪，斯为让非其义，所救非人，非所谓恶不仁者。

translations.literal: " Now the petty people not stretching the four limbs yet claiming others' rice—not benevolent in the extreme; yet Mu pushed and gave it to him, again saving his crime—this is yielding not its rightness, the rescue not the right person—not what is called hating the not benevolent."
translations.idiomatic: " A lazy man who claims another's field is deeply wrong; to reward him and void the law is misplaced kindness—not hating evil."

sentences.zh: 苟不恶不仁，安得为仁哉！

translations.literal: If one does not hate the not benevolent, how can it be called benevolence!
translations.idiomatic: Without hatred of evil there is no humanity.

sentences.zh: 苍梧浇娶妻而美，让於其兄；

translations.literal: The Jiao wife of Cangwu was beautiful and yielded to her elder brother;
translations.idiomatic: The man of Cangwu who gave his pretty wife to his brother

sentences.zh: 尾生笃信，水至不去而死；

translations.literal: Wei Sheng was steeped in faith—water came yet he did not go and died;
translations.idiomatic: and Wei Sheng who drowned keeping a tryst

sentences.zh: 直躬好直，证父攘羊；

translations.literal: Zhi Gong loved straightness, testifying against his father stealing a sheep;
translations.idiomatic: and Zhi Gong who bore witness against his father

sentences.zh: 申鸣奉法，尽忠於君而执其父。

translations.literal: Shen Ming upheld the law, exhausting loyalty to the lord yet seizing his own father.
translations.idiomatic: and Shen Ming who arrested his own father for the law

sentences.zh: 忠信直让，此四行者，圣贤之所贵也。

translations.literal: Loyalty, faith, straightness, yielding—these four conducts are what sages and worthies prize.
translations.idiomatic: were prized by the sages—each in its place.

sentences.zh: 然不贵苍梧之让，非让道也；

translations.literal: Yet one does not prize the yielding of Cangwu—it is not the way of yielding;
translations.idiomatic: We do not praise the Cangwu "yield"—it was not true yielding;

sentences.zh: 不取尾生之信，非信所也；

translations.literal: one does not take Wei Sheng's faith—it is not where faith applies;
translations.idiomatic: Wei Sheng's faith is not true faith;

sentences.zh: 不许直躬之直，非直体也；

translations.literal: one does not permit Zhi Gong's straightness—it is not the body of straightness;
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Gong's bluntness is not straightness;

sentences.zh: 不嘉申鸣之忠，非忠意也。

translations.literal: one does not praise Shen Ming's loyalty—it is not the intent of loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Ming's act is not loyalty in the right sense.

sentences.zh: 今牧犯而不校，还而不取，可以为难矣，未得为仁让也。

translations.literal: Now Mu offended yet did not reckon, returned yet did not accept—it can be called difficult, not yet obtained as benevolent yielding.
translations.idiomatic: Mu's patience is admirable but not yet benevolent yielding.

sentences.zh: 夫圣人以德报德，以直报怨，而牧欲以德报怨，非也。

translations.literal: The sage man with virtue repays virtue, with straightness repays resentment—yet Mu wishes with virtue to repay resentment—it is not right.
translations.idiomatic: The sage repays good with good and injury with justice; to repay injury with kindness is wrong.

sentences.zh: 必不得已，二者何从？

translations.literal: If it cannot be helped, of the two which to follow?
translations.idiomatic: If you must choose between them,

sentences.zh: 吾从孔子也。”〉

translations.literal: I follow Confucius." )
translations.idiomatic: I follow Confucius." )

sentences.zh: 赤烏五年，從郎中補太子輔義都尉，遷南海太守。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chiwu he was supplemented from gentleman of the palace to capital commandant who aids righteousness for the heir, promoted grand administrator of Nanhai.
translations.idiomatic: In 242 he rose from gentleman of the palace to capital commandant assisting the heir, then became prefect of Nanhai.

sentences.zh: 〈会稽典录曰：高凉贼率仍弩等破略百姓，残害吏民，牧越界扑讨，旬日降服。

translations.literal: ( Kuaiji dianlu states: The Gaoliang bandit chiefs Reng Nu and others broke and plundered the hundred surnames, cruelly injuring clerks and people; Mu crossed the boundary in sudden attack and punished; within ten days they surrendered in submission.
translations.idiomatic: ( The Kuaiji dianlu says he crossed into Gaoliang to crush bandit chiefs like Reng Nu and forced their surrender within ten days.

sentences.zh: 又揭阳县贼率曾夏等众数千人，历十馀年，以侯爵杂缯千匹，下书购募，绝不可得。

translations.literal: Again the Jieyang bandit chief Zeng Xia and others, hosts of several thousand persons, through more than ten years, with marquis rank and assorted silks a thousand bolts, issued edicts for purchase and recruitment—utterly could not be got.
translations.idiomatic: Jieyang chief Zeng Xia had defied Wu for over ten years despite posted rewards of nobility and silk—no one could catch him.

sentences.zh: 牧遣使慰譬，登皆首服，自改为良民。

translations.literal: Mu sent envoys to console and instruct; Zeng and the others all bowed heads in submission, on their own reforming to be good commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Mu sent envoys with fair words; Zeng Xia and his followers submitted and became law-abiding subjects.

sentences.zh: 始兴太守羊衜与太常滕胤书曰：“锺离子幹吾昔知之不熟，定见其在南海，威恩部伍，智勇分明，加操行清纯，有古人之风。

translations.literal: Grand administrator of Shixing Yang Dao wrote to Grand Master of Ceremonies Teng Yin: "Zhongli Zigan—I formerly knew him not thoroughly; fixing on seeing him in Nanhai, awe and favor toward the ranks, wisdom and courage clear and distinct, add conduct pure and clean, having the wind of the ancients."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Dao of Shixing wrote to Teng Yin, "I did not know Zhongli Mu well until I saw him rule Nanhai with equal parts awe and kindness, clear wit and courage, and spotless conduct—truly in the old style."

sentences.zh: ”其见贵如此。

translations.literal: His being valued was thus.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem he won.

sentences.zh: 在郡四年，以疾去职。〉

translations.literal: In the commandery four years, because of illness he left office. )
translations.idiomatic: After four years as prefect he resigned ill. )

sentences.zh: 還為丞相長史，轉司直，遷中書令。

translations.literal: Returning he was chief clerk of the chancellor, transferred director of integrity, promoted director of the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Back at court he became the chancellor's chief clerk, then director of integrity, then director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 會建安、鄱陽、新都三郡山民作亂，出牧為監軍使者，討平之。

translations.literal: It happened that the mountain people of Jian'an, Poyang, and Xindu three commanderies made disorder; he went out Mu as military overseer envoy, attacked and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: When hill folk of Jian'an, Poyang, and Xindu rebelled, he was named military overseer and crushed them.

sentences.zh: 賊帥黃亂、常俱籌出其部伍，以充兵役。

translations.literal: The bandit chiefs Huang Luan and Chang Ju presented their troops and hosts to fill military service.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel leaders Huang Luan and Chang Ju surrendered their followers for conscription.

sentences.zh: 封秦亭侯，拜越騎校尉。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed marquis of Qin village and appointed colonel of agile cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was made marquis of Qin village and colonel of agile cavalry.

sentences.zh: 永安六年，蜀併於魏，武陵五谿夷與蜀接界。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yongan, Shu was absorbed by Wei; the five streams Yi of Wuling bordered Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In 263 Shu fell to Wei; the five-streams tribes of Wuling bordered the former Shu frontier.

sentences.zh: 時論懼叛亂，乃以牧為平魏將軍，領武陵太守，往之郡。

translations.literal: Discussion at the time feared rebellion and disorder; thereupon Mu was made General Who Pacifies Wei, concurrent grand administrator of Wuling, and went to the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Court opinion feared revolt, so Zhongli Mu was named General Who Pacifies Wei and prefect of Wuling and sent to his post.

sentences.zh: 魏遣漢葭縣長郭純試守武陵太守，率涪陵民入蜀遷陵界，屯於赤沙，誘致諸夷邑君，或起應純，又進攻酉陽縣，郡中震懼。

translations.literal: Wei sent acting grand administrator of Wuling Guo Chun of Hanjia county to lead Fuling people into the Shu Qianling border, encamp at Red Sand, entice and summon the various Yi town chiefs—some rose in response to Chun; again he advanced to attack Youyang county; within the commandery there was shaken fear.
translations.idiomatic: Wei put Guo Chun of Hanjia in charge of Wuling, led Fuling settlers into the Qianling border region, camped at Red Sand, and rallied tribal headmen—some joined him and he pushed toward Youyang, throwing the county into panic.

sentences.zh: 牧問朝吏曰：「西蜀傾覆，邊境見侵，何以禦之？

translations.literal: Mu asked court clerks: "Western Shu has toppled; the border sees invasion—how shall we resist it?"
translations.idiomatic: Mu asked his staff, "Shu is gone and our border is threatened—how do we respond?"

sentences.zh: 」皆對曰：「今二縣山險，諸夷阻兵，不可以軍驚擾，驚擾則諸夷盤結。

translations.literal: " All answered: "Now the two counties are mountain perilous; the various Yi block arms—one cannot with an army startle and disturb them; if startled and disturbed then the various Yi will coil and bind together.
translations.idiomatic: " They said, "The terrain is rugged and the tribes are armed—do not provoke them with troops or they will unite against us.

sentences.zh: 宜以漸安，可遣恩信吏宣教慰勞。

translations.literal: It is fitting to use gradual peace; one may send clerks of favor and trust to proclaim instruction and console and labor.
translations.idiomatic: Move slowly: send trusted officers to talk them down.

sentences.zh: 」牧曰：「不然。

translations.literal: " Mu said: "It is not so.
translations.idiomatic: " Mu replied, "Wrong.

sentences.zh: 外境內侵，誑誘人民，當及其根柢未深而撲取之，此救火貴速之勢也。

translations.literal: The outer realm invades within, deceives and lures the hundred surnames—one ought while their root and stump are not yet deep to strike and take them—this is the momentum of fighting fire where speed is precious.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign agents are subverting our people—we must strike before the evil takes root, as in fighting a fire.

sentences.zh: 」敕外趣嚴，掾史沮儀者便行軍法。

translations.literal: " He ordered the outer offices to hurry strictness; any clerk who obstructed the marshalling was at once dealt with by military law."
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered full mobilization and told his staff that anyone who blocked the call-up would face military justice."

sentences.zh: 撫夷將軍高尚說牧曰：「昔潘太常督兵五萬，然後以討五谿夷耳。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the Yi Gao Shang spoke to Mu: "Formerly Grand Master of Ceremonies Pan led fifty thousand troops only then to punish the five streams Yi."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Shang, General Who Pacifies the Yi, warned him, "Pan Jun needed fifty thousand men to subdue the five streams."

sentences.zh: 是時劉氏連和，諸夷率化，今既無往日之援，而郭純已據遷陵，而明府以三千兵深入，尚未見其利也。

translations.literal: At that time the Liu clan was allied in peace; the various Yi led transformation; now there is already not the aid of former days, while Guo Chun already holds Qianling—and the enlightened prefect with three thousand troops goes deep—I have not yet seen its profit.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei once kept those tribes quiet; now there is no such ally, Guo Chun holds Qianling, and you would march in with three thousand—I see no gain in that.

sentences.zh: 」牧曰：「非常之事，何得循舊？

translations.literal: " Mu said: "An extraordinary affair—how can one follow the old?
translations.idiomatic: " Mu said, "These are extraordinary times—old rules do not apply.

sentences.zh: 」即率所領，晨夜進道，緣山險行，垂二千里，從塞上，斬惡民懷異心者魁帥百餘人及其支黨凡於余級，純等散，五谿平。

translations.literal: " At once he led those he commanded, morning and night advanced on the road, followed mountain peril in marching, nearly two thousand li, from the barrier heights upward, beheaded more than a hundred wicked commoners and chieftains who harbored different hearts and their partisans—in all more than a thousand ranks; Chun and the others scattered; the five streams were pacified."
translations.idiomatic: " He led his command on forced marches along two thousand li of mountain trails, stormed the heights, executed over a hundred rebel headmen and their followers—more than a thousand counted kills—and scattered Guo Chun's force, pacifying the five streams."

sentences.zh: 遷公安督、揚武將軍，封都鄉侯，徙濡須督。

translations.literal: He was promoted supervisor of Gong'an, General Who Displays Martial Might, enfeoffed village marquis of the capital district, transferred supervisor of Ruxu.
translations.idiomatic: He became Gong'an garrison commander, General Who Displays Martial Might, metropolitan village marquis, then moved to Ruxu command.

sentences.zh: 〈会稽典录曰：牧之在濡须，深以进取可图，而不敢陈其策，与侍中东观令硃育宴，慨然叹息。

translations.literal: ( Kuaiji dianlu states: When Mu was at Ruxu he deeply thought advance and seizure could be planned yet did not dare set forth his plan; drinking with Palace Attendant and director of the Eastern Pavilion Zhu Yu, he sighed with generous emotion.
translations.idiomatic: ( The Kuaiji dianlu says that at Ruxu he saw a chance to strike north but dared not speak; over wine with Zhu Yu he sighed heavily.

sentences.zh: 育谓牧恨於策爵未副，因谓牧曰：「朝廷诸君，以际会坐取高官，亭侯功无与比，不肯在人下，见顾者犹以於邑，况於侯也！

translations.literal: Yu said to Mu that he resented that strategy and noble rank did not match; therefore he said to Mu: "The various gentlemen of the court, by meeting fortune sit and obtain high office; the merit of a village marquis does not compare, unwilling to be below others—those who look on you still feel depressed—how much more you, marquis!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yu thought Mu chafed at his rank and said, "Courtiers ride luck to high posts; your village marquis title hardly matches your deeds—you must feel slighted."

sentences.zh: 」牧笑而答曰：「卿之所言，未获我心也。

translations.literal: " Mu smiled and answered: "What you have said has not gotten my heart.
translations.idiomatic: " Mu smiled and said, "You miss my meaning.

sentences.zh: 马援有言，人当功多而赏薄。

translations.literal: Ma Yuan had a saying: people ought to have much merit and thin reward.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yuan said men often deserve more reward than they receive.

sentences.zh: 吾功不足录，而见宠已过当，岂以为恨？

translations.literal: My merit is not enough to record, yet the favor shown me has passed what is fitting—how could I take that as resentment?
translations.idiomatic: My deeds hardly merit record, yet I have been over-rewarded—why should I resent that?

sentences.zh: 国家不深相知，而见害朝人，是以默默不敢有所陈。

translations.literal: The state does not deeply know each other, yet I am harmed by people at court—therefore I am silent and dare not have something to set forth.
translations.idiomatic: The throne does not know me well, and jealous men at court would harm me if I spoke—so I keep silent.

sentences.zh: 若其不然，当建进取之计，以报所受之恩，不徒自守而已，愤叹以此也。

translations.literal: If it were not so, I ought to establish plans for advance and seizure, to repay the grace I have received—not merely to guard myself alone—my angry sighs are for this.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise I would lay plans to repay your kindness instead of merely holding my post—that is what grieves me.

sentences.zh: 」育复曰：「国家已自知侯，以侯之才，无为不成。

translations.literal: " Yu again said: "The state already knows the marquis; with the marquis's talent, nothing done will not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhu Yu pressed, "The court knows your worth; with your ability nothing would fail.

sentences.zh: 愚谓自可陈所怀。

translations.literal: In my foolish view you ought yourself to set forth what you hold in your breast.
translations.idiomatic: Speak your mind, I say.

sentences.zh: 」牧曰：「武安君谓秦王云：『非成业难，得贤难；

translations.literal: " Mu said: "Lord Wu'an said to the King of Qin: It is not completing the enterprise that is hard—it is getting worthies that is hard;
translations.idiomatic: " Mu cited Bai Qi: finishing the work is not the hard part—finding worthy men is;

sentences.zh: 非得贤难，用之难；

translations.literal: it is not getting worthies that is hard—employing them is hard;
translations.idiomatic: finding them is not the hard part—using them is;

sentences.zh: 非用之难，任之难。

translations.literal: it is not employing them that is hard—trusting them is hard.
translations.idiomatic: using them is not the hard part—trusting them is.

sentences.zh: 』武安君欲为秦王并兼六国，恐授事而不见任，故先陈此言。

translations.literal: " Lord Wu'an wished for the King of Qin to annex the six states together; fearing that when entrusted with affairs he would not be trusted, therefore he first set forth these words.
translations.idiomatic: " Bai Qi warned Qin before taking the six states because he feared not being trusted once in command.

sentences.zh: 秦王既许而不能，卒陨将成之业，赐剑杜邮。

translations.literal: The King of Qin permitted him yet could not do it, in the end ruining the general's completed enterprise, bestowed the sword at Du post.
translations.idiomatic: Qin agreed yet failed him, ruined his work, and sent the suicide sword to Duyou.

sentences.zh: 今国家知吾，不如秦王之知武安，而害吾者有过范睢。

translations.literal: Now the state knows me not as the King of Qin knew Lord Wu'an, yet those who harm me surpass Fan Ju.
translations.idiomatic: The court knows me less than Qin knew Bai Qi, and my slanderers are worse than Fan Ju.

sentences.zh: 大皇帝时，陆丞相讨鄱阳，以二千人授吾，潘太常讨武陵，吾又有三千人，而朝廷下议，弃吾於彼，使江渚诸督，不复发兵相继。

translations.literal: In the time of the Great Emperor, Chancellor Lu in punishing Poyang gave me two thousand men; Grand Master of Ceremonies Pan in punishing Wuling—I again had three thousand men—yet the court held lower council, cast me off there, so that the various supervisors along the river did not again issue troops in succession.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Xun took Poyang I had two thousand men; when Pan Jun took Wuling I had three thousand—yet the court abandoned me and river garrisons sent no follow-up relief.

sentences.zh: 蒙国威灵自济，今日何为常。

translations.literal: I received the state's awesome numen and saved myself—how could today be as of old?
translations.idiomatic: I escaped ruin only by the state's grace—how could I gamble on that again today?

sentences.zh: 向使吾不料时度宜，苟有所陈，至见委以事，不足兵势，终有败绩之患，何无不成之有？」〉

translations.literal: Supposing I had not weighed the times and what was fitting, rashly had something to set forth, to the point of being entrusted with the affair yet lacking enough military force, in the end there would be the worry of defeat and rout—how could there be nothing that did not succeed?" )
translations.idiomatic: Had I pressed plans without timing or support, I would have courted disaster—how then could anything succeed?" )

sentences.zh: 復以前將軍假節，領武陵太守。

translations.literal: Again as former general with credentials of authority he held concurrent grand administrator of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: He was again named former general with the baton and concurrent prefect of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 家無餘財，士民思之。

translations.literal: The household had no surplus wealth; gentlemen and commoners thought of him.
translations.idiomatic: He left no fortune; officers and people mourned him.

sentences.zh: 子褘嗣，代領兵。

translations.literal: His son Hui succeeded, replacing him in leading troops.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhongli Hui inherited his rank and command.

sentences.zh: 〈会稽典录曰：牧次子盛，亦履恭让，为尚书郎。

translations.literal: ( Kuaiji dianlu states: Mu's second son Sheng also trod reverent yielding; he was gentleman of the palace in the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: ( The Kuaiji dianlu says second son Zhongli Sheng was humble and served as a gentleman of the palace.

sentences.zh: 弟徇领兵为将，拜偏将军，戍西陵，与监军使者唐盛论地形势，谓宜城、信陵为建平援，若不先城，敌将先入。

translations.literal: Younger brother Xun led troops as general, was appointed deputy general, garrisoned Xiling, and with military overseer envoy Tang Sheng discussed the lay of the land, saying Yicheng and Xinling ought to be supports for Jianping—if cities were not built first, the enemy would enter first.
translations.idiomatic: Brother Zhongli Xun commanded troops at Xiling and urged Tang Sheng that Yicheng and Xinling must be fortified as outworks of Jianping before the enemy could seize them.

sentences.zh: 盛以施绩、留平，智略名将，屡经於彼，無云當城之者，不然徇计。

translations.literal: Sheng held that Shi Ji and Liu Ping, wise in stratagem and famous generals, had repeatedly passed through there and there was no saying they ought to build walls there—he did not follow Xun's plan.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Sheng argued that Shi Ji and Liu Ping, seasoned strategists who knew the ground, had never insisted on fortifying there—so he rejected Xun's plan.

sentences.zh: 后半年，晋果遣将脩信陵城。

translations.literal: Half a year later Jin indeed sent a general to repair Xinling city.
translations.idiomatic: Six months later Jin sent engineers to fortify Xinling.

sentences.zh: 晋军平吴，徇领水军督，临陈战死。〉

translations.literal: When the Jin army pacified Wu, Xun led naval army supervisor, facing battle died in battle. )
translations.idiomatic: When Jin conquered Wu, Zhongli Xun commanded the navy as river garrison supervisor and died in battle. )

translations.literal: 【Appraisal】
translations.idiomatic: Appraisal

sentences.zh: 評曰：山越好為叛亂，難安易動，是以孫權不遑外御，卑詞魏氏。

translations.literal: The appraisal states: The mountain Yue are easy to make rebellion and disorder, hard to pacify and easy to move; therefore Sun Quan had no leisure to defend the outer realm and used humble words toward the house of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The appraiser says the hill Yue were ever restless, so Sun Quan could spare little force abroad and humbled himself toward Wei.

sentences.zh: 凡此諸臣，皆克寧內難，綏靜邦域者也。

translations.literal: All these various ministers were ones who could pacify inner disaster and quiet the domain of the state.
translations.idiomatic: These men quelled internal strife and steadied the realm.

sentences.zh: 呂岱清恪在公；

translations.literal: Lü Dai was pure and reverent in serving the public;
translations.idiomatic: Lü Dai was incorrupt and devoted to duty;

sentences.zh: 周魴譎略多奇；

translations.literal: Zhou Fang's deception and strategy had much of the strange;
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Fang's stratagems were singular;

sentences.zh: 鐘離牧蹈長者之規；

translations.literal: Zhongli Mu trod the gauge of the elder;
translations.idiomatic: Zhongli Mu walked the path of the gentleman;

sentences.zh: 全琮有當世之才，貴重於時，然不檢姦子，獲譏毀名云。

translations.literal: Quan Zong had talent for the age, was honored and weighty in his time, yet he did not restrain his wicked sons and met slander that destroyed his name, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Zong was a man of his time yet failed to curb his sons and lost his good name—so the verdict runs.
